first_n_text: This paper presents an analysis of vision-based abnormal red blood cell classification. The study aims to develop an automated system for the detection and classification of abnormal red blood cells using computer vision techniques. The proposed system utilizes image processing algorithms to extract relevant features from microscopic images of blood samples. These features are then used to train a machine learning model for the classification of normal and abnormal red blood cells. The performance of the system is evaluated using a dataset of blood samples with known abnormalities. The results show that the proposed system achieves high accuracy in the classification of abnormal red blood cells, demonstrating its potential for use in clinical settings for the early detection of blood disorders.

This paper explores the geometry of vectorial martingale optimal transportations and duality. The authors introduce a new notion of vectorial martingale optimal transportation and study its properties. They show that this notion is closely related to the classical notion of martingale optimal transportation and provide a duality result between the two. The authors also investigate the geometric properties of vectorial martingale optimal transportations and establish a connection with the theory of optimal transport. The paper concludes with several applications of the theory to various fields, including finance and economics. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding of vectorial martingale optimal transportations and their geometric properties.

Color image segmentation is an important task in computer vision and image processing. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for color image segmentation using adaptive particle swarm optimization (APSO) and fuzzy C-means (FCM) clustering. APSO is used to optimize the parameters of FCM, which helps in achieving better segmentation results. The proposed method adaptively adjusts the inertia weight and acceleration coefficients of APSO based on the fitness values of the particles. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms and shows promising results for color image segmentation.

The paper presents a multidimensional version of the Szemerédi theorem in the context of prime numbers. The Szemerédi theorem is a fundamental result in combinatorics that states that any subset of the natural numbers with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. The authors extend this result to multiple dimensions by considering subsets of the prime numbers with positive upper density. They prove that such subsets contain arbitrarily large multidimensional arithmetic progressions. The proof involves a combination of techniques from number theory, combinatorics, and ergodic theory. The multidimensional Szemerédi theorem in the primes has applications in various areas of mathematics, including additive combinatorics and number theory.

This paper presents the observation of empty liquids and equilibrium gels in a colloidal clay system. The authors use confocal microscopy to study the structure and dynamics of the colloidal clay particles. They find that at low concentrations, the system forms an empty liquid phase, where the particles are dispersed and do not form any structure. At higher concentrations, the system transitions to an equilibrium gel phase, where the particles form a network-like structure. The authors also investigate the effect of particle size and concentration on the formation of these phases. Overall, this study provides insights into the behavior of colloidal clay systems and contributes to our understanding of the self-assembly of colloidal particles.

This paper investigates the impact of inter-observer variability on the estimation of uncertainty in medical image segmentation. Uncertainty estimation is crucial for reliable and robust segmentation results, as it provides a measure of confidence in the accuracy of the segmentation. However, inter-observer variability, which refers to the differences in segmentation results obtained by different observers, can introduce additional uncertainty. The authors propose a method to quantify and account for inter-observer variability in uncertainty estimation. They evaluate their method on a dataset of medical images and compare the results with existing uncertainty estimation techniques. The findings demonstrate that considering inter-observer variability leads to more accurate and reliable

This paper presents a fast and fully octave convolutional neural network (CNN) for document image segmentation. Document image segmentation is a crucial step in many document analysis tasks, such as optical character recognition and document understanding. However, existing CNN-based methods for document image segmentation are often computationally expensive and require a large amount of memory. To address these issues, we propose a fully octave CNN architecture that leverages octave convolutional layers to capture multi-scale information efficiently. Our network achieves state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets while being significantly faster and more memory-efficient than existing methods. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed approach for document image segmentation.

Interactive image segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that requires accurately segmenting objects of interest from an image with user interaction. In this paper, we propose a fully convolutional two-stream fusion network for interactive image segmentation. The network consists of two streams: a segmentation stream and an interaction stream. The segmentation stream is responsible for generating initial segmentation masks, while the interaction stream is used to refine the segmentation masks based on user input. We introduce a novel fusion module that combines the outputs of the two streams to produce the final segmentation result. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed network achieves state-of-the-art performance in interactive image segmentation.

Deepfake technology has become increasingly sophisticated, making it difficult to detect manipulated content. In this paper, we propose a method for detecting deepfake-forged contents using a separable convolutional neural network (CNN) and image segmentation. The separable CNN is designed to capture both global and local features of the image, while the image segmentation technique helps to identify regions that have been manipulated. We evaluate our method on a large dataset of deepfake images and compare it with existing detection methods. The results show that our approach achieves high accuracy in detecting deepfake-forged contents, outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. This research contributes to the development of effective techniques for combating the spread of deepfake content.

This paper presents some results on the equivalence of multi-letter quantum finite automata (QFAs). QFAs are a model of computation that extend classical finite automata to include quantum operations. The authors investigate the problem of determining when two QFAs are equivalent, meaning that they accept the same language. They provide necessary and sufficient conditions for equivalence in the case of multi-letter QFAs, and show that the problem of equivalence is decidable for this class of machines. The authors also explore the relationship between equivalence of QFAs and the concept of bisimulation, a notion of behavioral equivalence in computer science. Overall, this paper contributes to our understanding of the computational power and behavior of multi-letter QFAs.

This paper investigates the sample complexity of auctions with side information. The authors analyze the number of samples required to achieve a certain level of accuracy in estimating the optimal auction outcome. They consider a setting where bidders have access to side information that can potentially improve their bidding strategies. The authors provide theoretical bounds on the sample complexity for different types of side information, including private values and correlated values. They also propose algorithms that exploit the side information to reduce the sample complexity. The results of this study have implications for the design and implementation of auctions in various domains, such as online advertising and spectrum auctions.

This paper presents a single chain slip-spring model for fast rheology simulations of entangled polymers on a graphics processing unit (GPU). The slip-spring model is a widely used approach for simulating the dynamics of entangled polymers, but its computational cost limits its application to large systems and long time scales. To overcome this limitation, the authors implement the slip-spring model on a GPU, which allows for massively parallel computations and significantly reduces the simulation time. The performance of the GPU implementation is evaluated by comparing the results with those obtained from a CPU-based implementation. The authors demonstrate that the GPU implementation achieves a speedup of several orders of magnitude, making it possible to simulate large systems and long time scales that were previously inaccessible. The proposed GPU-based slip-spring model provides a powerful tool for studying the rheological properties of entangled polymers and has the potential to advance our understanding of polymer processing and material design.

This paper presents a novel algorithm for approximately sampling elements with fixed rank in graded posets. Graded posets are partially ordered sets where each element is assigned a rank. The problem of sampling elements with fixed rank in graded posets is challenging due to the large number of elements and the need for efficient sampling methods. The proposed algorithm utilizes a combination of random sampling and importance sampling techniques to approximate the desired elements. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the algorithm compared to existing methods. The algorithm has potential applications in various domains, such as social network analysis and recommendation systems.

This paper investigates the Anderson localization phenomenon in one-dimensional elastic systems. Anderson localization refers to the phenomenon where disorder in a system leads to the confinement of electronic or vibrational states, preventing their propagation. The authors study the localization properties of elastic waves in one-dimensional disordered systems using numerical simulations. They find that the presence of disorder leads to the localization of elastic waves, with the localization length depending on the strength of the disorder. The authors also analyze the effect of different types of disorder on the localization properties. The results of this study contribute to the understanding of the Anderson localization phenomenon in elastic systems and have potential applications in the design of materials with desired wave propagation properties.

Computer stereo vision is a key technology for enabling autonomous driving systems to perceive and understand the surrounding environment. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the state-of-the-art techniques and algorithms used in computer stereo vision for autonomous driving. The paper discusses the fundamental principles of stereo vision, including camera calibration, disparity estimation, and depth map generation. It also explores various approaches for handling challenges such as occlusions, dynamic scenes, and low-texture regions. Additionally, the paper examines the integration of stereo vision with other perception sensors, such as LiDAR and radar, to enhance the robustness and accuracy of autonomous driving systems. The paper concludes with a discussion on the future directions and potential advancements in computer stereo vision for autonomous driving.

Pneumothorax is a potentially life-threatening condition that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment. In this paper, we propose a deep learning-based approach for pneumothorax segmentation in chest X-ray images. We utilize a convolutional neural network architecture to automatically identify and segment regions of pneumothorax in the images. Our model is trained on a large dataset of annotated chest X-ray images and achieves high accuracy in pneumothorax segmentation. We evaluate the performance of our model on a separate test dataset and compare it with other state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately predicting pneumothorax regions, which can aid radiologists in the diagnosis and treatment of this condition.

This paper presents a fish recognition system that combines robust feature selection, image segmentation, and geometrical parameter techniques using Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms. The proposed system aims to accurately identify fish species based on their visual characteristics. The feature selection process is performed to extract the most discriminative features from the fish images. Image segmentation is then applied to separate the fish from the background, improving the accuracy of the recognition process. Geometrical parameters such as length, width, and aspect ratio are extracted to further enhance the recognition accuracy. The extracted features and geometrical parameters are used as inputs to both ANN and DT algorithms for classification.

This paper explores the connections between subriemannian geometry and algebraic geometry. Subriemannian geometry is a branch of differential geometry that studies geometric structures on submanifolds that are not necessarily Riemannian. Algebraic geometry, on the other hand, studies the geometry of solutions to polynomial equations. The paper discusses how techniques from algebraic geometry can be applied to study subriemannian structures, and vice versa. It also explores the potential applications of these connections in various fields, such as robotics and control theory. Overall, this paper aims to bridge the gap between subriemannian geometry and algebraic geometry, and highlight the potential for cross-fertilization between these two fields.

This paper presents a study on the design of robust controllers for regular linear systems with infinite-dimensional exosystems. The authors propose a new approach based on the use of a robust control framework to handle uncertainties and disturbances in the system. The proposed controllers are designed to ensure stability and performance in the presence of these uncertainties. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical simulations and comparisons with existing methods. The results show that the proposed controllers outperform existing methods in terms of stability and performance. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of robust control for regular linear systems with infinite-dimensional exosystems.

This paper presents a novel approach for semantic segmentation of point clouds using a boundary-aware geometric encoding. Point clouds are a popular representation for 3D data, but their irregular and unordered nature makes semantic segmentation challenging. The proposed method addresses this challenge by encoding geometric information about the boundaries of objects in the point cloud. This encoding is then used as input to a deep neural network for semantic segmentation. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The boundary-aware geometric encoding provides a valuable representation for point cloud segmentation tasks and has the potential to improve performance in various applications such as autonomous driving and robotics.

Video segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision that involves partitioning a video into different regions based on their semantic content. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for video segmentation using Convolutional Gated Recurrent Networks (CGRNs). CGRNs combine the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture both spatial and temporal information in videos. We introduce a gating mechanism that allows the network to selectively update and forget information at each time step, improving the model's ability to handle long-range dependencies. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it to state-of-the-art methods. The experimental results demonstrate that our CGRN model achieves competitive performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This extended technical report presents the Extended LTLvis Motion Planning interface, a tool for visualizing and interacting with Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) specifications in the context of motion planning. The interface allows users to define LTL formulas and visualize their satisfaction on a given motion planning problem. It provides a user-friendly graphical interface that enables users to specify LTL formulas using a combination of predefined temporal operators and user-defined predicates. The interface also allows users to visualize the satisfaction of the LTL formulas on a given motion planning problem by generating a graph that shows the evolution of the system's state over time. The report describes the design and implementation of the interface, as well as its integration with existing motion planning algorithms. It also presents several case studies that demonstrate the effectiveness and usability of the interface in various motion planning scenarios.

This paper presents a deep learning approach for estimating the recurrence of atrial fibrillation (AF) using an end-to-end framework. AF is a common cardiac arrhythmia that can lead to serious health complications. Accurate estimation of AF recurrence is crucial for guiding treatment decisions and monitoring patient outcomes. The proposed approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract features from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model temporal dependencies. The model is trained on a large dataset of ECG recordings from patients with known AF recurrence outcomes. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed deep learning approach achieves high accuracy in estimating AF recurrence, outperforming traditional machine learning methods.

In this paper, we present a theoretical and experimental study on the time reversal of light by linear dispersive filtering near atomic resonance. We demonstrate that by carefully designing the dispersion properties of a medium, it is possible to reverse the temporal order of a light pulse. We show that this effect can be achieved by exploiting the dispersive properties of an atomic medium near its resonance frequency. We provide a detailed theoretical analysis of the underlying physical mechanisms and derive the conditions for achieving time reversal. We also present experimental results that confirm the theoretical predictions. Our findings have important implications for the field of optical signal processing and may lead to the development of novel devices for controlling the temporal properties of light pulses.

This paper explores the benefits of linear conditioning with metadata for image segmentation. Image segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision, and recent advancements have shown the effectiveness of deep learning models for this task. However, these models often require a large amount of labeled data for training, which can be expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages metadata information to improve the performance of image segmentation models. Specifically, we introduce a linear conditioning mechanism that incorporates metadata features into the model's architecture. We conduct experiments on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy.

Data augmentation is a common technique used in machine learning to improve the generalization performance of models. However, it is often assumed that the augmented data should be representative of the unseen test data, leading to the use of domain generalization techniques. In this paper, we challenge this assumption and propose a new perspective on data augmentation. We argue that in certain cases, unseen domain generalization is unnecessary and that data augmentation can still improve model performance even if the augmented data does not perfectly match the test data distribution. We provide empirical evidence to support our argument and demonstrate that data augmentation can be effective even when the augmented data is not representative of the unseen test data. Our findings suggest that researchers and practitioners should reconsider the role of unseen domain generalization in data augmentation and explore alternative approaches that focus on improving model robustness and generalization rather than matching the test data distribution.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in the field of medical imaging, as it enables accurate diagnosis and treatment planning. However, existing methods for medical image segmentation often suffer from slow inference times due to the use of deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) as encoders. In this paper, we propose a novel architecture called LeViT-UNet, which combines the efficiency of the Vision Transformer (ViT) with the accuracy of the U-Net for medical image segmentation. Our approach replaces the CNN encoder in the traditional U-Net with a lightweight ViT encoder, resulting in faster inference times without sacrificing segmentation performance. We evaluate our method on two publicly available medical image segmentation datasets and demonstrate that LeViT-UNet achieves comparable or even better segmentation accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods, while significantly reducing inference times. Our findings suggest that LeViT-UNet has the potential to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of medical image segmentation in clinical practice.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of crossovers induced by discrete-time quantum walks. Quantum walks are a fundamental concept in quantum information theory and have been extensively studied in the context of continuous-time quantum walks. However, the study of discrete-time quantum walks and their potential to induce crossovers has received less attention. In this paper, we present a theoretical framework for analyzing crossovers induced by discrete-time quantum walks and provide numerical simulations to support our findings. We show that discrete-time quantum walks can indeed induce crossovers and discuss the implications of this phenomenon for quantum information processing. Our results contribute to a better understanding of discrete-time quantum walks and their potential applications in quantum computing and quantum algorithms.

Land cover segmentation is a crucial task in remote sensing applications, as it provides valuable information for various environmental and urban planning studies. However, the performance of land cover segmentation algorithms can be affected by differences in satellite sensors and acquisition conditions. In this paper, we propose a domain adaptation approach to improve land cover segmentation across different satellites. We first train a segmentation model on a source dataset from one satellite and then adapt it to a target dataset from a different satellite using domain adaptation techniques. Specifically, we employ a domain adversarial neural network to align the feature distributions between the source and target domains. Experimental results on two publicly available land cover datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed approach in improving land cover segmentation accuracy across different satellites.

Semantic video segmentation is a challenging task that requires accurate and efficient processing of large amounts of video data. In this paper, we propose TapLab, a fast framework for semantic video segmentation that leverages compressed-domain knowledge. TapLab utilizes a tap-based approach to efficiently process video frames by tapping into compressed-domain information. We introduce a TapNet architecture that combines a tap-based encoder-decoder network with a compressed-domain feature extractor. Our experiments demonstrate that TapLab achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and speed on various benchmark datasets. Furthermore, we show that TapLab is robust to compression artifacts and can effectively handle videos with different compression levels.

This paper proposes a bidirectional recurrent neural network (RNN)-based approach for few-shot learning in the context of 3D medical image segmentation. Few-shot learning is a challenging task in medical imaging due to the limited availability of annotated data. The proposed approach leverages the bidirectional nature of RNNs to capture both forward and backward dependencies in the input data. The model is trained on a small number of labeled samples and then fine-tuned on a larger unlabeled dataset using a self-training strategy. Experimental results on a publicly available 3D medical image segmentation dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. The bidirectional RNN-based few-shot learning approach shows promise for improving the segmentation accuracy of 3D medical images with limited labeled data.

This paper proposes a novel approach for image segmentation using deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with spatial regularization, volume, and star-shape priori. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by incorporating spatial information, volume constraints, and star-shape priori into the CNN architecture. The spatial regularization helps to preserve the spatial coherence of the segmented regions, while the volume constraint ensures that the segmented regions have a consistent volume. The star-shape priori is used to guide the segmentation process by enforcing a star-shaped boundary for each segmented region. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method has the potential to be applied in various applications such as medical image analysis, object recognition, and scene understanding.

BoundarySqueeze: Image Segmentation as Boundary Squeezing

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. Traditional approaches to image segmentation often rely on pixel-level classification or region-based methods, which can be computationally expensive and may not accurately capture the boundaries between different objects. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to image segmentation called BoundarySqueeze, which formulates the task as a boundary squeezing problem. 

 The key idea behind BoundarySqueeze is to iteratively squeeze the boundaries between different objects in an image until they are sufficiently separated. This is achieved by applying a series of squeezing operations that gradually push the boundaries towards the interior of the objects. We introduce a new boundary squeezing operator that combines both local and global information to effectively capture the shape and context of the objects.

This paper presents a novel approach for sub 20 nm silicon patterning and metal lift-off using thermal scanning probe lithography (t-SPL). The t-SPL technique utilizes a heated probe to locally heat the resist material, enabling precise control over the patterning process. The authors demonstrate the feasibility of sub 20 nm patterning by fabricating silicon nanostructures with dimensions as small as 10 nm. Additionally, the paper explores the use of t-SPL for metal lift-off, a critical step in the fabrication of nanoscale devices. The results show that t-SPL can achieve high-resolution metal patterning with excellent lift-off efficiency. Overall, this work presents a promising approach for sub 20 nm silicon patterning and metal lift-off, offering potential applications in nanoelectronics and nanophotonics.

IPatch is a novel approach to generating adversarial patches that can be remotely applied to images to deceive deep learning models. Unlike previous methods that require physical access to the target image, IPatch leverages the power of generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create patches that can be applied remotely. The proposed method consists of two stages: patch generation and patch application. In the patch generation stage, a GAN is trained to generate patches that are visually similar to the target image but contain adversarial perturbations. In the patch application stage, the generated patch is applied to the target image remotely, fooling the deep learning model into misclassifying the image. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of IPatch in evading state-of-the-art deep learning models, highlighting the potential security risks associated with remote adversarial attacks.

StructBoost is a boosting method that aims to predict structured output variables. Boosting is a popular machine learning technique that combines weak learners to create a strong learner. However, most boosting methods are designed for predicting scalar variables and are not suitable for structured output variables, such as sequences or trees. StructBoost addresses this limitation by introducing a novel framework that can handle structured output variables. The proposed method leverages the concept of structured loss functions and uses a structured version of AdaBoost to iteratively train weak learners. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of StructBoost in predicting structured output variables, outperforming existing methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

Semantic segmentation is a crucial task in computer vision that involves assigning a label to each pixel in an image. Deep structured models have shown promising results in this task, but training them can be computationally expensive. In this paper, we propose an efficient piecewise training approach for deep structured models for semantic segmentation. Our method divides the training process into multiple stages, where each stage focuses on a specific region of the image. We also introduce a novel loss function that encourages the model to learn both local and global context information. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive performance while significantly reducing training time and computational resources.

Medical image segmentation plays a crucial role in various clinical applications, such as disease diagnosis and treatment planning. However, obtaining a large-scale dataset with fully annotated labels for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust medical image segmentation on small-scale data with incomplete labels. Our method leverages the concept of self-training and semi-supervised learning to effectively utilize the available labeled and unlabeled data. We introduce a consistency regularization term to encourage the model to produce consistent predictions on unlabeled data, which helps improve the segmentation performance. Additionally, we propose a novel uncertainty estimation technique to identify the most uncertain predictions and prioritize them for expert annotation, thereby iteratively improving the quality of the labeled data.

This paper explores the concept of quantitative automata under probabilistic semantics. It presents a formal framework for modeling and analyzing systems that exhibit both probabilistic and quantitative behavior. The paper introduces a new class of automata called quantitative automata, which extend traditional automata models to incorporate quantitative aspects such as costs, rewards, and probabilities. The authors define the semantics of quantitative automata using probabilistic transition systems and provide algorithms for analyzing their behavior. The paper also discusses applications of quantitative automata in various domains, including performance analysis, optimization, and decision-making. Overall, this paper contributes to the understanding and development of quantitative automata as a powerful tool for modeling and analyzing complex systems.

This paper provides an introduction to stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). SPDEs are a class of equations that involve both random and deterministic components, making them a powerful tool for modeling complex systems with inherent uncertainty. The paper begins by introducing the basic concepts of probability theory and stochastic processes, which form the foundation for understanding SPDEs. It then discusses the different types of SPDEs, including linear and nonlinear equations, and provides examples of their applications in various fields such as finance, physics, and biology. The paper also covers numerical methods for solving SPDEs, including finite difference and Monte Carlo methods. Overall, this paper serves as a comprehensive introduction to the theory and applications of SPDEs, making it a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners in the field.

In this paper, we investigate the consistency of matter models with asymptotically safe quantum gravity. We consider a class of matter models that are coupled to gravity and study their behavior in the ultraviolet regime. We show that these matter models can be consistently coupled to asymptotically safe quantum gravity, which is a theory that remains well-defined at high energies. We analyze the renormalization group flow of the matter models and find that they exhibit a non-trivial fixed point in the ultraviolet regime. This fixed point allows for a consistent coupling between matter and gravity, providing a promising framework for studying the physics of the early universe and black holes. Our results suggest that matter models with asymptotically safe quantum gravity can provide a consistent description of fundamental interactions at high energies.

This paper presents a novel approach for left atrial segmentation in 3D gadolinium enhanced-MRI using dilated convolutions in neural networks. Left atrial segmentation is an important task in the diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation. Traditional methods for left atrial segmentation rely on manual annotation, which is time-consuming and subjective. In this study, we propose a deep learning model that utilizes dilated convolutions to capture both local and global information in the MRI images. We evaluate our model on a dataset of 100 patients and compare its performance with other state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that the proposed model achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach for image inpainting of high-resolution textures using convolutional neural network (CNN) texture synthesis. Image inpainting is the process of filling in missing or corrupted parts of an image. Traditional methods for image inpainting often struggle with high-resolution textures due to their complex and intricate patterns. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based approach that leverages the power of deep learning to generate realistic and visually coherent inpainted textures. Our method consists of two main steps: texture synthesis and texture transfer. First, we train a CNN to learn the underlying texture patterns from a set of high-resolution texture images.

This paper presents a novel approach for learning to segment objects in images using only image-level supervision. Traditional methods for image segmentation require pixel-level annotations, which are expensive and time-consuming to obtain. In this work, we propose a framework that leverages the power of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to learn to segment objects using only image-level labels. Our approach involves training a CNN to predict object presence in an image, and then using this information to generate pseudo pixel-level annotations. These pseudo annotations are then used to fine-tune the CNN, resulting in improved segmentation performance. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that it achieves competitive results compared to state-of-the-art methods that rely on pixel-level annotations.

Few-shot segmentation is a challenging task in computer vision, where the goal is to segment objects in an image given only a few annotated examples. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Self-Guided and Cross-Guided Learning (SGCL) for few-shot segmentation. SGCL leverages both self-guided and cross-guided learning to improve the segmentation performance. Self-guided learning uses the available annotated examples to guide the segmentation process, while cross-guided learning utilizes information from other images to further refine the segmentation results. We evaluate SGCL on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art few-shot segmentation methods. The experimental results demonstrate that SGCL achieves superior performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and generalization ability.

Image Compositing for Segmentation of Surgical Tools without Manual Annotations

 Abstract:

Segmentation of surgical tools in medical images is a crucial step in computer-assisted surgery and robotic surgery systems. However, manual annotation of surgical tools is time-consuming and requires expert knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for segmenting surgical tools without the need for manual annotations. Our method utilizes image compositing techniques to generate synthetic images of surgical tools with known ground truth segmentations. These synthetic images are then used to train a deep learning model for surgical tool segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach for soft-thresholding in both discrete and continuous-time domains with dynamic inputs. The proposed method utilizes a dynamic thresholding function that adapts to the changing input signal. The discrete-time soft-thresholding algorithm is derived using a recursive formulation, while the continuous-time soft-thresholding algorithm is obtained by solving a differential equation. The performance of the proposed algorithms is evaluated through simulations and compared with existing methods. The results demonstrate that the dynamic soft-thresholding approach outperforms traditional methods in terms of signal recovery and noise reduction. This research contributes to the field of signal processing by providing a new framework for soft-thresholding that can effectively handle dynamic inputs.

Phase unwrapping is a critical step in many imaging applications, including interferometry and synthetic aperture radar. In this paper, we propose a novel isotropic inverse-problem approach for two-dimensional phase unwrapping. Our method is based on the assumption that the phase is smooth and can be represented as a sum of a low-frequency component and a high-frequency component. We formulate the phase unwrapping problem as a regularized least-squares optimization problem and solve it using an iterative algorithm. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world data. Our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and robustness, making it a promising solution for phase unwrapping in various imaging applications.

This paper proposes a novel approach for source-free domain adaptation in the context of image segmentation. Traditional domain adaptation methods rely on labeled source domain data to train a model that can generalize to a target domain. However, in many real-world scenarios, obtaining labeled source domain data is expensive or impractical. To address this limitation, we introduce a source-free domain adaptation framework that leverages unlabeled source and target domain data. Our approach combines a self-training strategy with a consistency regularization loss to encourage the model to produce consistent predictions on both domains. We evaluate our method on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate its effectiveness in improving segmentation performance on the target domain without using any labeled source domain data.

This paper presents a Matlab implementation of a machine vision algorithm for evaluating ballast degradation. The algorithm utilizes image processing techniques to analyze images of ballast samples and determine the level of degradation. The implementation includes preprocessing steps such as image enhancement and noise reduction, as well as feature extraction and classification steps. The algorithm is tested on a dataset of ballast images and the results are compared to manual evaluations. The results show that the algorithm is able to accurately evaluate ballast degradation, with a high level of agreement with manual evaluations. The Matlab implementation provides a user-friendly interface for researchers and practitioners to easily apply the algorithm to their own ballast samples.

This paper presents ACNN, a full resolution deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) for medical image segmentation. ACNN is designed to address the challenges of segmenting medical images with high resolution and complex structures. The network architecture consists of multiple convolutional layers followed by upsampling layers to preserve the full resolution of the input image. ACNN also incorporates skip connections to enable information flow between different levels of the network. The proposed network is trained using a combination of pixel-wise cross-entropy loss and Dice loss. Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that ACNN achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency.

Food image segmentation is an important task in computer vision, with applications in food recognition, dietary analysis, and meal tracking. However, existing food image segmentation datasets are limited in terms of scale and diversity, which hinders the development and evaluation of robust segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we present a large-scale benchmark dataset for food image segmentation, called FoodSeg-250K, which contains 250,000 food images with pixel-level annotations. The dataset covers a wide range of food categories and includes diverse variations in terms of appearance, lighting conditions, and occlusions. We also propose a novel evaluation metric, called FoodIoU, which takes into account the specific challenges of food image segmentation. We evaluate several state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms on the FoodSeg-250K dataset and provide detailed analysis and insights into their performance.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in medical imaging analysis, as it plays a crucial role in diagnosis and treatment planning. However, obtaining large amounts of annotated medical images for training deep learning models is often challenging due to the limited availability of expert annotations. In this paper, we propose a semi-supervised few-shot learning approach for medical image segmentation. Our method leverages a small amount of labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data to improve the performance of the segmentation model. We introduce a novel few-shot learning framework that combines a pre-trained segmentation network with a few-shot learning module. The few-shot learning module is trained on a small labeled dataset and then fine-tuned on a large unlabeled dataset using a self-training strategy.

This paper presents a convolutional neural network (CNN) based approach for the segmentation of medical imaging data. The segmentation of medical images is a crucial step in various clinical applications, such as tumor detection and organ delineation. Traditional segmentation methods often rely on handcrafted features and require extensive manual intervention. In contrast, CNNs have shown promising results in various computer vision tasks, including image segmentation. In this work, we propose a CNN architecture specifically designed for medical image segmentation. We evaluate our approach on a dataset of medical images and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

In medical image segmentation tasks, the presence of corrupted labels and domain shift can significantly degrade the performance of deep learning models. This paper proposes a novel Cross-denoising Network (CDN) to address these challenges. CDN consists of two denoising modules: a label denoising module and a feature denoising module. The label denoising module utilizes a self-supervised learning strategy to estimate the true labels from the corrupted labels. The feature denoising module employs a domain adaptation technique to align the feature distributions between the source and target domains. Experimental results on a medical image segmentation dataset demonstrate that CDN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness against corrupted labels and domain shift.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of signal focusing through active transport. Active transport is a process by which cells actively move molecules or ions across their membranes, against their concentration gradient, using energy from ATP. The authors propose a theoretical model to explain how active transport can lead to signal focusing, where a signal is concentrated in a specific region of a cell or tissue. They demonstrate the validity of their model through computational simulations and provide experimental evidence from previous studies that support their findings. The paper concludes by discussing the potential implications of signal focusing through active transport in various biological processes, such as cell signaling and development. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the mechanisms underlying signal focusing and highlights the importance of active transport in cellular communication.

This paper presents a novel approach for left atrium segmentation in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using a combination of global shape priors and local intensity priors. The proposed method utilizes a mixture modeling framework to integrate both types of priors, allowing for accurate and robust segmentation of the left atrium. The global shape priors are learned from a training dataset using a shape model, while the local intensity priors are learned using an autoencoder. The mixture model is then trained using a combination of the shape and intensity priors, and is used to segment the left atrium in new MRI images. Experimental results on a dataset of cardiac MRI images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness. The proposed approach has the potential to improve clinical diagnosis and treatment planning for patients with left atrium abnormalities.

This paper proposes a novel approach for semantic image segmentation using loss max-pooling. The traditional max-pooling operation in convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is modified to incorporate loss information during training. The loss max-pooling operation selects the maximum value not only based on the input feature maps but also on the corresponding loss maps. This allows the network to focus on regions with high loss, improving the segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed loss max-pooling approach outperforms traditional max-pooling and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy. The proposed approach provides a promising direction for improving semantic image segmentation in CNNs.

The paper "Log-Determinant Divergences Revisited: Alpha--Beta and Gamma Log-Det Divergences" presents a comprehensive study of log-determinant divergences, specifically the alpha-beta and gamma log-det divergences. These divergences have been widely used in various fields, including machine learning and information theory. The paper provides a detailed analysis of the properties and characteristics of these divergences, including their relationship with other well-known divergences. The authors also propose new formulations and extensions of these divergences, and demonstrate their usefulness in practical applications. The paper concludes with experimental results that validate the effectiveness of the proposed divergences in various scenarios. Overall, this paper contributes to a better understanding and utilization of log-determinant divergences in statistical analysis and machine learning.

This paper provides an introduction to the concept of many worlds in quantum computation. Many worlds is a theoretical interpretation of quantum mechanics that suggests the existence of multiple parallel universes. The paper begins by explaining the basics of quantum mechanics and the measurement problem, which is the challenge of understanding how quantum systems collapse into a single state upon measurement. It then introduces the many worlds interpretation as a possible solution to this problem, describing how it posits that the universe splits into multiple branches with each possible outcome of a measurement. The paper also discusses the implications of many worlds for quantum computation, highlighting how it can be used to explain the power of quantum computers and the phenomenon of quantum parallelism. It concludes by discussing the challenges and criticisms of the many worlds interpretation and suggesting avenues for future research in this area.

This paper presents experimental constructions of binary matrices with good peak-sidelobe distances. The peak-sidelobe distance is a measure of the quality of a binary matrix, with a larger distance indicating better performance. The authors propose two different constructions based on different mathematical techniques. The first construction is based on the theory of finite fields, while the second construction is based on the theory of combinatorial designs. The experimental results show that both constructions yield binary matrices with significantly better peak-sidelobe distances compared to existing constructions. These results have important implications for applications such as radar and sonar signal processing, where binary matrices with good peak-sidelobe distances are crucial for accurate detection and classification.

In this paper, we investigate the relationship between nonlocality and the central geometry of dimer algebras. Dimer algebras are a class of noncommutative algebras that arise in the study of quantum mechanics and have applications in various areas of physics and mathematics. We introduce a notion of nonlocality for dimer algebras and show that it is closely related to the central geometry of these algebras. Specifically, we prove that a dimer algebra is nonlocal if and only if its central geometry is nontrivial. We also provide explicit examples to illustrate our results and discuss their implications for the study of dimer algebras and their applications. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the interplay between nonlocality and the central geometry of dimer algebras, and may have implications for the development of new mathematical and physical models.

FusionNet is a deep fully residual convolutional neural network designed for image segmentation in connectomics. Connectomics is the study of neural connections in the brain, and accurate segmentation of neural structures is crucial for understanding brain function. FusionNet combines multiple levels of information from different image modalities to improve segmentation accuracy. The network architecture includes residual connections to alleviate the vanishing gradient problem and enable efficient training. Experimental results on connectomics datasets demonstrate that FusionNet outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed network has the potential to advance the field of connectomics and contribute to our understanding of the brain.

Deformable image registration (DIR) is a fundamental task in medical image analysis that involves aligning two or more images by estimating a deformation field. Traditional approaches to DIR rely on optimization-based methods that require manual tuning of parameters and are computationally expensive. In recent years, there has been growing interest in learning-based approaches to DIR, which aim to automatically learn the registration process from data. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of learning-based DIR methods, including their perspective, modules, bilevel training, and future directions. The authors discuss the advantages and limitations of learning-based DIR and highlight the key challenges in this field. They also propose a novel bilevel training framework for learning-based DIR, which combines the strengths of optimization-based and learning-based methods.

This paper presents a novel approach for automating the design of deep learning methods for biomedical image segmentation. The proposed method utilizes a genetic algorithm to search for optimal network architectures and hyperparameters. The algorithm is guided by a fitness function that evaluates the performance of the network on a validation dataset. The approach is demonstrated on two different biomedical image segmentation tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on both. The results show that the automated design process can effectively discover high-performing deep learning methods for biomedical image segmentation, saving time and effort compared to manual design. The proposed approach has the potential to accelerate the development of deep learning methods for biomedical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to iris recognition using a database of iris images obtained in visible light using a smartphone camera. The proposed method leverages the advancements in smartphone camera technology to capture high-quality iris images in visible light, eliminating the need for specialized iris recognition hardware. The paper describes the image acquisition process and the preprocessing steps applied to enhance the quality of the iris images. The iris recognition algorithm is based on a combination of feature extraction and matching techniques, which are optimized for visible light iris images. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving high recognition accuracy on a dataset of iris images captured using a smartphone camera. The findings of this study have significant implications for the development of iris recognition systems that can be easily deployed using widely available smartphone technology.

This paper proposes a novel approach called Error Corrective Boosting (ECB) for training fully convolutional networks (FCNs) with limited data. FCNs have shown great success in various computer vision tasks, but they often require a large amount of labeled data for training. In scenarios where labeled data is scarce, traditional training methods may lead to overfitting and poor generalization. ECB addresses this issue by iteratively training an ensemble of FCNs and correcting their errors using a boosting algorithm. The proposed method effectively leverages the limited labeled data by focusing on the most challenging samples and gradually improving the performance of the FCNs. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that ECB outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, especially when the training data is limited.

Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) have been widely used for structured prediction tasks in natural language processing and computer vision. However, CRFs suffer from limitations such as the need for handcrafted features and the inability to capture long-range dependencies. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to address these limitations by formulating CRFs as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). We show that by modeling the CRF as an RNN, we can learn the feature representations directly from the data, eliminating the need for manual feature engineering. Additionally, the RNN formulation allows for the capture of long-range dependencies, improving the performance of the CRF. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and demonstrate that our method outperforms traditional CRFs in terms of accuracy and efficiency.

SkrGAN: Sketching-rendering Unconditional Generative Adversarial Networks for Medical Image Synthesis

Abstract:
Medical image synthesis plays a crucial role in various applications, such as data augmentation, disease diagnosis, and surgical planning. However, generating realistic medical images is challenging due to the limited availability of labeled data and the complexity of medical imaging modalities. In this paper, we propose SkrGAN, a novel unconditional generative adversarial network (GAN) framework for medical image synthesis. SkrGAN combines the advantages of sketching and rendering techniques to generate high-quality medical images from random noise. The sketching module generates a rough outline of the desired medical image, while the rendering module refines the sketch by adding detailed textures and structures. We train SkrGAN on a large dataset of labeled medical images and evaluate its performance on various medical imaging tasks, including MRI, CT, and ultrasound image synthesis.

The Standard Model of particle physics has been successful in explaining the fundamental particles and their interactions. However, there are several phenomena that cannot be explained within this framework, such as the existence of dark matter, the matter-antimatter asymmetry in the universe, and the hierarchy problem. This paper reviews the current status of physics beyond the Standard Model, including theories such as supersymmetry, extra dimensions, and grand unified theories. It discusses the experimental evidence for these theories and the challenges in testing them. The paper also explores the implications of physics beyond the Standard Model for cosmology and astrophysics. Overall, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current understanding and open questions in physics beyond the Standard Model.

Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is a neurosurgical procedure that involves the implantation of electrodes in specific regions of the brain to treat various neurological disorders. Accurate localization of these electrodes is crucial for effective treatment and post-operative management. In this paper, we propose an automatic localization method for deep stimulation electrodes using a trajectory-based segmentation approach. The proposed method utilizes the trajectory information of the electrode leads obtained from pre-operative imaging data to segment and localize the electrodes in post-operative imaging data. The method involves three main steps: trajectory extraction, trajectory-based segmentation, and electrode localization. Experimental results on a dataset of DBS patients demonstrate the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method in localizing deep stimulation electrodes.

This paper explores the concept of relative entailment among probabilistic implications. It presents a formal framework for reasoning about the relative strength of probabilistic implications, based on the notion of probabilistic entailment. The paper introduces a measure of relative entailment, which quantifies the degree to which one probabilistic implication is stronger than another. The measure is shown to satisfy several desirable properties, such as transitivity and monotonicity. The paper also discusses the relationship between relative entailment and other notions of entailment, such as logical entailment and probabilistic implication. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed measure in capturing the relative strength of probabilistic implications in various domains.

In medical imaging, accurate segmentation of organs and tumors is crucial for diagnosis and treatment planning. However, obtaining fully labeled datasets for training deep learning models is often challenging and time-consuming. In this paper, we propose a novel framework called DoDNet that leverages multiple partially labeled datasets to learn to segment multi-organ and tumors. Our approach combines a self-training strategy with a dual-objective learning scheme to effectively utilize the available labeled and unlabeled data. We evaluate DoDNet on a large dataset of abdominal CT scans and demonstrate its superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Our results show that DoDNet achieves high segmentation accuracy while reducing the reliance on fully labeled datasets, making it a promising tool for medical image segmentation tasks.

This paper introduces a new measure of dependence called Copula Correlation, which is an extension of Pearson's Correlation. The Copula Correlation is designed to address the limitations of Pearson's Correlation, such as its sensitivity to outliers and non-linear relationships. The proposed measure is based on copulas, which are mathematical functions that describe the dependence structure between random variables. The Copula Correlation is shown to be a more equitable measure of dependence, as it treats all variables equally and is not affected by the marginal distributions of the variables. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the Copula Correlation and its properties, and demonstrates its effectiveness through various examples and simulations. Overall, the Copula Correlation offers a more robust and fair measure of dependence compared to existing methods.

This paper presents an in-situ Raman study of laser-induced graphene oxidation. Laser-induced graphene (LIG) is a promising material for various applications due to its unique properties. However, the oxidation of LIG can significantly affect its performance. In this study, we investigate the oxidation process of LIG using Raman spectroscopy. We observe the formation of various oxygen-containing functional groups on the LIG surface during the oxidation process. The intensity of the D and G bands in the Raman spectra decreases with increasing oxidation time, indicating the reduction of sp2 carbon content.

This paper presents U-Time, a fully convolutional network (FCN) designed for time series segmentation, specifically applied to sleep staging. Sleep staging is the process of classifying different stages of sleep based on physiological signals. U-Time utilizes a modified version of the U-Net architecture, which has been successful in image segmentation tasks. The network is trained on a large dataset of polysomnography recordings and achieves state-of-the-art performance in sleep staging. The authors also propose a novel loss function that incorporates both pixel-wise and sequence-wise information, improving the segmentation accuracy. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of U-Time in accurately segmenting sleep stages, making it a valuable tool for sleep research and clinical applications.

Image segmentation is a fundamental task in computer vision that involves partitioning an image into meaningful regions. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for image segmentation using a hierarchical merge tree. The merge tree is constructed by iteratively merging adjacent regions based on a similarity measure. We introduce a new similarity measure that takes into account both color and texture information. The merge tree is then used to guide the segmentation process, where regions are merged or split based on the tree structure. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in producing accurate and visually pleasing segmentations.

Semantically-consistent image-to-image translation is a challenging task in computer vision, as it requires generating images that not only capture the style of a given input image but also maintain the semantic content. In this paper, we propose a novel framework called Sem-GAN that addresses this problem. Sem-GAN consists of two main components: a semantic segmentation network and a generative adversarial network (GAN). The semantic segmentation network is used to extract the semantic information from the input image, which is then used to guide the image translation process. The GAN is responsible for generating the translated image, while the semantic information is used as a constraint to ensure the semantic consistency between the input and output images. We evaluate our approach on several benchmark datasets and compare it with state-of-the-art methods.

Salient object detection is a challenging task in computer vision, especially in the wild where images contain complex backgrounds and multiple objects. In this paper, we propose a novel approach called Inner and Inter Label Propagation (IILP) for salient object detection in the wild. The proposed method leverages both inner and inter label propagation to effectively capture the salient regions in an image. Inner label propagation is used to refine the initial saliency map by considering the local consistency of saliency values. Inter label propagation, on the other hand, utilizes the global consistency of saliency values across multiple images to further enhance the saliency map. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed IILP method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the privacy and security of medical data pose significant challenges in developing accurate and reliable segmentation algorithms. In this paper, we propose BUNET, a blind medical image segmentation method based on secure UNET. BUNET leverages the UNET architecture for accurate segmentation while incorporating privacy-preserving techniques to ensure the confidentiality of sensitive medical data. We evaluate the performance of BUNET on a dataset of medical images and compare it with existing segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that BUNET achieves competitive segmentation accuracy while maintaining the privacy and security of medical data.

This paper presents an application of cascaded 3D fully convolutional networks (FCNs) for medical image segmentation. The proposed method utilizes a series of FCNs to iteratively refine the segmentation results, improving the accuracy and robustness of the segmentation process. The cascaded architecture allows for the incorporation of contextual information from multiple scales, enhancing the segmentation performance. The method is evaluated on a dataset of medical images and compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation approaches. The results demonstrate that the cascaded 3D FCNs achieve superior segmentation accuracy and outperform existing methods in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency. The proposed method has the potential to significantly improve medical image segmentation tasks and contribute to advancements in clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

The abstract for the academic paper titled "Anomalous Hall Effect in Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te Composite System" discusses the investigation of the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) in a composite system composed of Ge(1-x-y)Pb(x)Mn(y)Te. The AHE is a phenomenon where a transverse voltage is generated in the presence of a magnetic field, and it has been extensively studied in various materials. In this study, the authors synthesized the composite system using a combination of molecular beam epitaxy and ion implantation techniques. They then characterized the material using X-ray diffraction, scanning electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy. The AHE measurements were performed using a four-probe method in a temperature range of 5-300 K and magnetic fields up to 9 T. The results showed a clear AHE signal in the composite system, indicating the presence of a nontrivial Berry curvature. The authors also observed a strong dependence of the AHE on the Mn concentration, suggesting a significant role of the Mn dopants in the AHE mechanism.

Multi-focus image fusion is an important technique in image processing that aims to combine multiple images with different focus levels into a single image with enhanced overall focus. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-focus image fusion method based on similarity characteristics. The proposed method first calculates the similarity between each pixel in the input images using a similarity measure. Then, a weight map is generated based on the similarity values, which is used to assign weights to each pixel in the input images. Finally, the weighted average of the input images is computed to obtain the fused image. Experimental results on a dataset of multi-focus images demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both visual quality and objective evaluation metrics.

Medical image segmentation is a crucial task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, accurately segmenting medical images is challenging due to the complex and diverse nature of the images. In this paper, we propose a novel network architecture called ET-Net, which stands for Edge-aTtention guidance Network. ET-Net utilizes an attention mechanism to guide the segmentation process by focusing on the edges of the objects in the image. This attention mechanism helps the network to better capture the boundaries and details of the objects, leading to improved segmentation accuracy. We evaluate the performance of ET-Net on several medical image segmentation tasks, including brain tumor segmentation and lung nodule segmentation.

This paper presents a novel segmentation network called Crosslink-Net, which utilizes a double-branch encoder architecture to fuse vertical and horizontal convolutions for improved segmentation performance. The proposed network consists of two encoder branches, each employing a different convolutional operation, and a decoder branch for feature fusion and segmentation. The vertical branch focuses on capturing vertical contextual information, while the horizontal branch captures horizontal contextual information. The two branches are then fused at multiple levels to enhance the overall segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on various benchmark datasets demonstrate that the Crosslink-Net outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation networks in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed network has the potential to advance the field of semantic segmentation in computer vision applications.

DeepIGeoS is a deep interactive geodesic framework proposed for medical image segmentation. The framework combines the advantages of deep learning and geodesic distance-based methods to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. It incorporates a deep neural network architecture that is trained on a large dataset of annotated medical images. The geodesic distance-based method is used to refine the segmentation results by incorporating spatial information and enforcing smoothness constraints. The proposed framework is evaluated on various medical image datasets and compared with state-of-the-art segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that DeepIGeoS achieves superior segmentation accuracy and efficiency, making it a promising tool for medical image analysis and clinical applications.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of overlapping resonances in open quantum systems. Resonances occur when the energy of a system matches the energy of an external driving force, leading to enhanced response. In open quantum systems, resonances can overlap due to the presence of multiple driving forces or the coupling of different modes. The authors develop a theoretical framework to describe the dynamics of overlapping resonances and analyze their effects on the system's behavior. They demonstrate that overlapping resonances can lead to complex and non-intuitive phenomena, such as the emergence of new resonant states and the modification of resonance widths. The findings have implications for various fields, including quantum information processing and quantum sensing, where understanding and controlling resonances is crucial.

Thalamus segmentation is an important task in neuroimaging research, as it allows for the identification and analysis of specific thalamic nuclei. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-contrast MRI approach to thalamus segmentation. Our method combines T1-weighted, T2-weighted, and diffusion-weighted images to improve the accuracy and robustness of thalamus segmentation. We first preprocess the images to enhance the contrast and remove noise. Then, we use a combination of intensity-based and atlas-based segmentation techniques to delineate the thalamus boundaries. We evaluate our method on a dataset of 50 subjects and compare the results with manual segmentations performed by experts.

In this paper, we study the structure and cohomology of moduli spaces of formal modules. We begin by introducing the notion of a formal module and its associated moduli space. We then investigate the structure of these moduli spaces, including their dimension and smoothness properties. Next, we compute the cohomology groups of these moduli spaces using various techniques, such as the Leray spectral sequence and the Grothendieck spectral sequence. We also establish connections between the cohomology of moduli spaces of formal modules and other areas of algebraic geometry, such as the cohomology of moduli spaces of vector bundles. Finally, we apply our results to the study of deformation theory and the classification of formal groups.

This paper presents an end-to-end trainable deep active contour model for automated image segmentation, specifically focusing on delineating buildings in aerial imagery. The proposed model combines the strengths of deep learning and active contour models to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation results. The model is trained using a large dataset of aerial imagery and ground truth annotations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also discusses the potential applications of the proposed model in various domains, such as urban planning and disaster response. Overall, this work contributes to the field of automated image segmentation by introducing a novel approach that can effectively delineate buildings in aerial imagery.

Medical image segmentation is a critical task in computer-aided diagnosis and treatment planning. However, it is challenging due to the high variability and complexity of medical images. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for robust medical image segmentation using cooperative training and latent space data augmentation. Our method leverages the power of multiple models trained on different subsets of the data to improve segmentation accuracy. Additionally, we introduce a latent space data augmentation technique that generates realistic and diverse augmented samples to enhance the generalization capability of the models. We evaluate our approach on a large dataset of medical images and compare it with state-of-the-art segmentation methods.

In this paper, we study the existence and properties of interior bubbling solutions for the critical Lin-Ni-Takagi problem in dimension 3. The Lin-Ni-Takagi problem is a nonlinear elliptic equation involving the critical Sobolev exponent. We consider the case where the equation is posed in a bounded domain with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We prove the existence of interior bubbling solutions, which are solutions that concentrate their energy at a finite number of interior points. We also investigate the behavior of these solutions near the concentration points and establish some qualitative properties. Our results provide new insights into the behavior of critical nonlinear elliptic equations in dimension 3 and contribute to the understanding of interior bubbling phenomena.

This paper presents a method for fast edge detection using structured forests. The proposed method leverages the power of structured forests, which are ensembles of decision trees, to efficiently detect edges in images. The authors introduce a novel edge detection algorithm that combines the strengths of structured forests with a fast edge filtering technique. The algorithm achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of both accuracy and speed. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of their approach through extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing edge detection methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper explores the use of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for mapping vulnerable populations. Vulnerable populations, such as those affected by poverty, natural disasters, or health crises, often face unique challenges that require targeted interventions. Traditional methods of mapping these populations can be time-consuming and resource-intensive. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that leverages AI algorithms to analyze various data sources, including satellite imagery, social media posts, and demographic data, to identify and map vulnerable populations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through case studies in different contexts, including disaster response and public health planning. Our findings suggest that AI-based mapping can provide valuable insights for policymakers and aid organizations to better understand and address the needs of vulnerable populations.

This paper presents a scalable variational inference algorithm for log-supermodular models. Log-supermodular models are a class of probabilistic models that arise in various applications, including social network analysis and combinatorial optimization. The proposed algorithm leverages the structure of log-supermodular models to develop an efficient variational inference procedure. The algorithm is scalable to large datasets and can handle high-dimensional parameter spaces. Experimental results on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed algorithm compared to existing methods. Overall, this paper contributes to the field of variational inference by providing a scalable solution for log-supermodular models.
