Many neurons exhibit morphological plasticity, altering the shape and connectivity of their dendritic spines in response to physiological cues. Here, we show that chronic activation of endogenous signaling pathways downstream of bone morphogenetic protein (BMP) receptors leads to the rapid loss of dendritic spines in cortical neurons in culture and dendritic simplification in neurons in mouse brain slices. Signaling was specific to BMP ligands because Activin did not produce these effects and because the BMP pathway inhibitors, Dorsomorphin and DMH1, blocked the signaling. Interestingly, the effects of BMP signaling in culture were blocked by inhibitors of histone deacetylase (HDAC) activity, including sodium butyrate and trichostatin A, but not by the kinase inhibitors, suggesting a link between BMP signaling and HDAC activity. Moreover, BMP ligands induced recruitment of HDAC2 and 3 to the nucleus as shown by immunofluorescence and pull-down assays. Inhibiting HDAC activity blocked the ability of BMP ligands to simplify dendritic structures, to cause a decrease in synaptic puncta number, and to cause an increase in the percentage of neurons with a single punctum.

We present a conditional random field (CRF) model and a deep learning-based feature learning approach for hyperspectral image (HSI) segmentation. The CRF model is a traditional statistical model used for image segmentation tasks, where pixel-level labels are predicted based on the features of the pixels and the spatial dependencies between the pixels. The deep learning-based feature learning approach is used to learn a low-dimensional feature representation of the hyperspectral data, which is then used as input to the CRF model. The proposed approach was evaluated on the Indian Pines hyperspectral dataset, and achieved a segmentation accuracy of 94.4%.

 The CRF model uses a probabilistic approach to capture the spatial dependencies between pixels, and is trained using a maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) approach. The deep learning-based feature learning approach is based on a convolutional neural network (CNN), which is trained using a supervised learning approach.

We present a novel gated conditional random field (CRF) loss for weakly supervised semantic image segmentation, which combines the benefits of supervised and unsupervised training while mitigating their respective shortcomings. Whereas supervised segmentation typically provides precise but sparse training labels, unsupervised methods exhibit smooth but inconsistent predictions. By conditioning the CRF on a mask obtained from a segmentation confidence map, we provide stronger guidance to the model where it is more uncertain, producing more consistent and accurate segmentations. Furthermore, our method is able to explicitly leverage additional supervision, despite its noise, to further improve performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on the PASCAL VOC 2012 semantic image segmentation benchmark, obtaining state-of-the-art performance. Code is available at https://github.com/NVlabs/paced-crf.

Recent advances in deep learning have achieved remarkable performance in semantic image segmentation. However, training deep segmentation models requires a large amount of labeled images, which are difficult to obtain. Data augmentation is a useful technique to generate more training samples by applying different transformations to the original images. Most data augmentation methods focus on image-level augmentation, which applies the same transformation to all objects in an image. This is a limitation for semantic image segmentation, as it cannot increase the diversity of objects in an image. In this paper, we introduce a new data augmentation method called ObjectAug, which performs object-level data augmentation for semantic image segmentation.

In this paper, we propose a new method for segmenting meaningful objects in SAR images. The proposed method is based on a multi-scale non-local active contour model. The non-local operation is implemented by a Gaussian weighted distance map, which can describe the long-range spatial dependence with a single parameter. In the multi-scale framework, a series of Gaussian weighted distance maps are employed as the internal energy and the external energy of the active contour model, respectively. By minimizing the energy function, a series of active contours are generated in different scales. Finally, the segmentation result is obtained by combining the information from the multi-scale active contours.

Academic biographies on Wikipedia undergo preferential editing, with notable professors more likely to have biographies than less notable ones, and with those biographies more likely to be of higher quality, according to a study published in the Journal of Documentation. These findings run counter to the notion of Wikipedia as a democratic encyclopedia and raise questions about the information found in the world's most popular reference work.

 The research team, from the University of Pittsburgh and Wikitonia, analyzed 7,634 academic biographies from the English-language Wikipedia on February 7, 2017, linking each subject to the highest-ranked institution with which they were associated and categorizing each subject by discipline. They then determined each subject's "notability" by whether or not they had their own academic biography on Wikipedia and calculated a "quality" score for each subject based on the average number of words in their biography and the average number of references linked to that biography.

 The researchers found that subjects associated with institutions ranked among the top 100 universities in the world were more likely to have a Wikipedia biography than those affiliated with institutions that rank outside the top 1000. A similar trend was observed in subjects who had earned a PhD or other doctoral degree and those who had not.

We present a fully convolutional two-stream fusion network (TCN) for real-time interactive image segmentation. The TCN is designed to leverage the benefits of both feed-forward and recurrent neural networks while avoiding their limitations. Our network is composed of two streams: a feed-forward convolutional neural network (CNN) stream and a recurrent convolutional neural network (RCNN) stream. The CNN stream provides initial segmentation results, which are refined by the RCNN stream in a coarse-to-fine fashion. The two streams are combined at the feature level using a concatenation layer, which allows the network to leverage the strengths of both streams and improve the segmentation performance. We evaluate the TCN on the interactive image segmentation benchmark ISBI 2017 and achieve competitive results with state-of-the-art methods.

We show how to construct optimal image segmentations using particle methods. Our approach is based on minimization of a functional that trades off between segmenting pixels correctly and minimizing the gradient of the resulting segmentation. This functional is a Sobolev gradient, that is, the sum of the gradients of all pixels, weighted by a per-pixel smoothness term. We propose to approximate this Sobolev gradient by a particle system, and show that, under an approximation scheme, the global minimizer of the particle system corresponds to the optimal segmentation. Furthermore, we show how to efficiently solve the particle system using a block-coordinate descent algorithm. We evaluate our method on the benchmark datasets of the 2016 CAMELYON challenge, and show that it compares favorably to state-of-the-art segmentation methods, while being simpler, faster, and requiring less parameter tuning.

Fast panoptic segmentation is a fundamental task for many computer vision applications. Existing methods usually concatenate prediction branches for different categories, yielding a huge increase in model size and computation. In this work, we propose a lightweight and efficient approach for fast panoptic segmentation, termed AinnoSeg. Specifically, we introduce a weight-shared U-Net whose output channels are dynamically determined by the intermediate features. A key insight is that the hierarchical features in the U-Net can be naturally aligned with the panoptic segmentation hierarchy (i.e., instance-level, stuff-level, and thing-level), and therefore the U-Net can be adapted to different parts of the hierarchy with different output channels. This adaptability allows us to selectively enlarge the capacity for hard instances (e.g., small stuff) while keeping a small model size for easy instances (e.g., large things).

Recent progress in artificial intelligence has enabled the automation of various agriculture-related tasks, such as crop and weed detection. However, creating a large and diverse dataset for training deep learning models can be a time-consuming and laborious process, which can hinder the development of accurate and robust models. In this paper, we present a data generation framework that automatically creates a large and diverse dataset for training deep learning models to detect crops and weeds. Our framework utilizes a combination of image segmentation, edge detection, and geometric projection algorithms to generate synthetic training data that closely resembles real-world images. Furthermore, our framework can rapidly create datasets of various sizes and crop types, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experiments, showing that our framework can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of deep learning models for crop and weed detection.

We present a technique for improving the performance of random walker image segmentation and registration algorithms. Our method involves precomputing and storing intermediate results for a fixed set of input parameters. By storing these precomputed results, we are able to significantly reduce the time required to compute the final result for any given input image. We find that our method is particularly useful for segmentation and registration problems that involve large images or a large number of images. Our method is adaptable in the sense that it can be used with any random walker algorithm that utilizes a graphical model representation. We present experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of our method on a number of different images.

We consider the problem of predicting a structured output variable y, which depends on an input x through a possibly nonlinear, parametric mapping function f(x, θ). In many applications, such as chemoinformatics and bioinformatics, one has a very large number of samples, and an abundance of features, but only a small number of training examples for each class of interest. For example, a dataset of 100,000 molecules may have activity data for 1000 molecules with a particular biological response, but only 10 examples for a rarer phenotype. We propose a boosting approach which is applicable in such cases. We handle the parametric nature of the mapping by using a Gaussian process (GP) surrogate model. This allows us to construct a distribution over the space of possible functions, given a particular input.

Automatic image segmentation is a classic problem in image processing, with many applications in areas such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and biological imaging. In this paper, we present an automatic image segmentation method based on dynamic region merging. Our method combines the advantages of both region-based and edge-based segmentation methods, while avoiding the drawbacks of each. The proposed method is efficient, automatic, and does not require any user interaction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a variety of images, including those with complex shapes and textures. We also compare our method to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods, and show that it performs favorably in terms of segmentation quality and efficiency.

In this note, we present a simple proof of the quantitative subspace theorem of Gurvits and Barnum [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 52, 3457 (2006)]. The proof relies on only the basic properties of random matrices and the tail bounds for the eigenvalues of random matrices. Compared to the original proof, the new proof is more self-contained and does not rely on the probabilistic method.

 The quantitative subspace theorem of Gurvits and Barnum is a key tool in the study of the capacity of random networks.

Recent works have shown that the attention mechanism can be applied to convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to improve performance on image recognition tasks. We observe that these works mostly focus on applying attention mechanism within the last few layers of CNNs, where the spatial dimensions of the feature maps are already very small, and the attention mechanism can effectively "attend" to the most important features. However, in the early layers of CNNs where the feature maps are still very large, the attention mechanism is often not effective, as there are simply too many positions for the attention to focus on. In this work, we propose a simple and effective approach to overcome this limitation. We introduce a new type of layer that we call the "AttentionBoost" layer, which works by combining the feature maps from the previous layer with the attention maps generated by a single-layer CNN. This allows the attention mechanism to effectively attend to the most important features in the early layers of the network, even when the feature maps are very large.

Encoder Fusion Network with Co-Attention Embedding (EFN-CAE) is a new deep learning architecture designed for the task of referring image segmentation. EFN-CAE leverages a fusion of high-level and low-level features learned by two encoders to highlight the referred objects in the image. Furthermore, a co-attention mechanism is introduced to model the relationship between the referring expression and the image, generating spatial attention weights to focus on the relevant areas. The referred regions are obtained by fusing global and local features of the image using the attention weights. In addition, we introduce a novel referredness measure to weigh the importance of each referred region. This measure is learned jointly with the segmentation network.

In this paper, we propose a novel image segmentation enhancement technique based on active contour and topological alignments. Our method combines the advantages of both approaches to achieve accurate and robust segmentation results. We begin by initializing an active contour model using a set of seed points and then iteratively refine the segmentation by considering topological alignments between the contour and the image. The topological alignments are computed using a novel graph-based approach that considers the local structure of the image. The proposed method is evaluated on a variety of images and compared to state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques. The results show that the proposed method achieves improved segmentation accuracy and robustness, especially in challenging images with complex structures and textures.

We propose a Performance analysis of an improved MUSIC Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) estimator, which utilizes the MUSIC algorithm for DoA estimation of a uniform linear array (ULA). In our improved algorithm, we employ the eigenvalue decomposition (EVD) and the Toeplitz structure of the correlation matrix to reduce the computational complexity, as well as a new technique to select the parameter in the MUSIC algorithm, which is based on the use of the Cauchy prior. By using these improvements, we enhance the performance of the MUSIC DoA estimator. In this paper, we analyze the performance of our improved algorithm by calculating the root mean square error (RMSE) and the mean absolute error (MAE) between the DoAs estimated by the improved algorithm and the true angles. The performance analysis is carried out by varying the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and the number of sources. The results show that our improved algorithm provides a significant performance improvement in comparison to the conventional MUSIC algorithm, especially for low SNR values and a small number of sources.

We present an approach to spontaneous noise spectroscopy of atomic vapor that aims to suppress the dominant source of noise in the scheme, namely, the noise induced by the vacuum environment of the atomic sample. The approach is based on a combination of common mode rejection and a optimized cavity configuration. We describe the noise reduction mechanisms and discuss the coherence properties of the scheme. The presented approach can be implemented in a variety of platforms, including optically trapped atoms and cells. 

 We analyze a scheme for spontaneous noise spectroscopy of atomic vapor based on a cavity-enhanced coherent population trapping resonance. We propose a novel configuration that enables efficient common mode rejection of the vacuum noise, which is the dominant noise source in the scheme.

We present results of gamma-ray spectroscopy measurements of positron annihilation in glycerol performed at beam line 16C1 of the Institute for Basic Science, UNIST. Gamma-ray emission from the title compound was detected in the energy range up to 3100 MeV. The analysis of the obtained spectra allowed us to determine the lifetime and positron energy spectrum of the positronium (Ps) state in glycerol. No evidence of the quasi-free Ps state was found. We compare the results with recent ab initio calculations of the positron affinity and the positron state properties in glycerol. Good agreement between the experimental results and theoretical predictions was obtained.

We propose a fast fully octave convolutional neural network (FCN) for document image segmentation. Our network dynamically scales the convolutional kernels by a factor of two between every two layers, which we refer to as octave convolution. This approach reduces the parameters by a factor of two per layer and shrinks the computational cost, yet it does not reduce the receptive field of the network. We evaluate our method on the publicly available ICDAR 2015 document image segmentation benchmark. Our network achieves a higher accuracy with a significantly reduced computational cost compared to the state-of-the-art methods. Our network also reduces the running time for training and testing by a factor of 2.1 and 3.4, respectively, compared to the second fastest method in the benchmark.

Urban sense segmentation, which aims to assign semantic labels to pixels in urban scenes, is a fundamental task for many applications such as autonomous driving and robotic perception. Recent advances in this field have achieved remarkable performance mainly based on two-stream architectures that separately learn global and local features. However, these methods usually rely on heuristic designs to fuse global and local features, which limits their performance. In this paper, we propose a hybrid transformer to learn adaptive global-local representations for urban sense segmentation. Specifically, we design a global-local attention module to model the interactions between global and local features, allowing the model to focus on different aspects of the input in a self-adaptive manner. Furthermore, a hierarchical transformer structure is introduced to capture the contextual information at multiple levels of granularity.

We perform the first large-scale analysis of petition growth and success rates on the UK No. 10 Downing Street website, spanning over 13 years (from February 2006 to June 2019) and including 415,348 petitions. We find that the number of signatures received increases with petition age, and this relationship is steeper for more recent years. We also find a significant linear relationship between the mean signature rate per day and the median number of signatures received, which implies that getting signatures quickly is important for petition success. Next, we show that a small number of petitions receive a large fraction of the signatures, and that this is more pronounced in recent years. Finally, we show that success rates have decreased over time and that a "threshold model" where a fixed number of signatures leads to an outcome is not supported by the data. However, a logistic regression model with petition signature velocity as a significant predictor of success is supported by the data.

We study a system of weakly coupled clusters, describing a disordered material with metallic and insulating states, by means of using numerical linked-cluster expansion, which is based on an exact treatment of all cluster excitations. Previously discovered metal-insulator transition line in the parameter space of the model is reproduced. We find a new type of transition line, which ends up in a critical point, at which a metal-insulator quantum phase transition takes place. Near the critical point, both types of transitions are of second order. Using an additional parameter, we fine-tune the system to a new region of the phase diagram, where the metallic and insulating states are separated by a first-order transition. We provide an explanation of the nature of the metallic state and the metal-insulator transition in terms of existing concepts of the theory of disordered materials.

We introduce a formalism of a segment-phrase table (SPT) for semantic segmentation, visual entailment and paraphrasing tasks. It captures the universal hierarchy of semantic propositions of entities, their attributes and relationships in a fine-grained and compositional manner. A neural network is trained to induce an SPT from unsupervised video and image captions, where each row corresponds to a phrase in a caption and each column corresponds to a segment in a video or image. The cell entries capture the likelihood of the phrase explaining the segment based on a similarity metric. An SPT factorizes the likelihood as a product of the individual phrase and segment probabilities, which enables the evaluation of paraphrases by simply summing their respective entries. We show that an SPT can be used for visual entailment, where an SPT entry supports or refutes the presence of a phrase in a given segment.

Recent progress in 3D medical image segmentation has benefited from both convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformer-based architectures, but their individual limitations hinder performance and efficiency. To address these limitations, we present CoTr, a simple and efficient hybrid architecture that combines the strengths of CNN and transformer-based models. Our approach dynamically allocates the tasks of feature extraction and segmentation across the two architectures based on the image size, enabling efficient training and inference on large images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on three challenging 3D medical image segmentation tasks: abdominal organ segmentation from CT, pulmonary nodule segmentation from CT, and hippocampus segmentation from T1-weighted MRI. Our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on all three datasets, significantly improving over previous methods, while being more efficient for segmentation on large images. Code is available at https://github.com/ interpreteur/CoTr.

Fuzzy clustering method is used for segmentation of vertebrae in T1-weighted spinal magnetic resonance (MR) images. In this method, the membership functions are optimized by Genetic Algorithm (GA). The input parameters for the GA are the gray levels and their neighboring pixels. The output is the set of fuzzy rules that define the membership functions. The fuzzy rules are then used for segmentation of the vertebrae. The proposed method is evaluated on 20 T1-weighted spinal MR images.

Recent works have shown that encoders based on pre-trained Transformers, particularly ViTs, set new standards for the quality of the learned representations for natural images, outperforming traditional convolutional neural networks. In this work, we adapt Transformers for medical image segmentation. In particular, we propose to use Transformers as encoders, predicting segmentations as a whole image classification. To adapt the Transformers to this task, we modify the classification layer to take into account the label hierarchy and handle overlapping segments. We present a new Transformer encoder based on ViT, called TransUNet, that outperforms the current state-of-the-art methods for segmentation on multiple benchmarks for both 2D and 3D medical images. Our code is available at https://github.com/DPichenaux/TransUNet.

We study the complexity of optimizing multicell coordinated beamforming with rate outage constraint, which maximizes the sum-rate of the network subject to a reliability requirement. We first present a polynomial time algorithm to solve this non-convex problem to global optimality when the number of users is equal to or larger than the number of base stations. This algorithm is based on a novel semi-definite programming (SDP) formulation of the problem, and on a block coordinate descent (BCD) method. Then, we propose a low-complexity greedy algorithm that achieves a near-optimal performance with significantly reduced computational complexity. The proposed greedy algorithm is based on a novel approximation of the optimal beamforming matrix, and on a thresholding technique that allows us to select the most beneficial users for cooperation. Finally, we present numerical results that illustrate the performance of the proposed algorithms in terms of sum-rate and outage probability, and that demonstrate the significant reduction in computational complexity achieved by the greedy algorithm.

We present a new type of rheological measurement of dry granular flows using an instrumented pin tumbler. In this device, a cylindrical bin is rotated with a constant speed, and a pin is attached to the center of the bottom of the bin. Granular material is placed in the bin, and as the bin rotates, the material is agitated and descends slowly toward the bottom. During this process, the structure of the material changes from an ordered stack of disks to a random state and then to an ordered state again as it passes through the bin. We measure the stress in the vertical direction as a function of the shear stress using load cells attached to the bin and the pin, respectively. The measured stress versus shear stress curves exhibit power-law dependence at high shear stresses, and the power-law exponents are equal to the average interparticle friction coefficient $\mu_I$, which is determined using a rotating disk device.

Recent works have shown that few-shot learning (FSL), where training datasets are significantly reduced, can generalize well when the support set has a similar distribution to the query set. However, for medical image segmentation, creating training datasets that capture the distribution of rare diseases is often costly and time-consuming, whereby a segmentation model trained with such datasets can generalize poorly to hospital scenarios, where patients with different rare diseases need to be segmented. In this work, we propose a self-supervision approach to train a segmentation model without requiring any annotation. Specifically, we train the model with a sparse-coding loss that forces the model to reconstruct the original image from its segmented image. We then enforce the consistency between the original and reconstructed image using a cycle-consistent loss, which does not require any ground-truth segmentation. To improve the segmentation quality, we introduce superpixels to capture global structures in medical images.

We calculate presupernova neutrino emissivities from the evolution of massive stellar models with masses ranging from 8 to 40 $M_{\odot}$. Special attention is paid to the effects of mixing length, convection, and hyperonization. Our models suggest that the presupernova neutrino emissivity becomes independent of mass and nearly equal to the one previously calculated by Itoh et al. (2001) for a 15 $M_{\odot}$ model at the time of core collapse when convection and hyperonization are considered. The presupernova emission, which lasts for about 10$^{5}$ seconds, carries away 1.3% of the star's rest mass as neutrinos. This corresponds to 1.1 baryon number conservation violations (BCVs) for a 40 $M_{\odot}$ model, which could be detectable by the next generation of neutrino detectors. We also examine the dependence of the neutrino emissivities on the mixing length, the enhancement factor of the convection, and the choice of the opacity. 

  Enhanced convection does not change the total emission but leads to an increased neutrino luminosity at the beginning and end of the presupernova evolution.

We perform the first systematic investigation of the universality of the luminosity-metallicity (L-Z) and mass-metallicity (M-Z) relations for compact galaxies at 0 < z < 3. We compile a sample of ~104 galaxies with stellar mass < 10^9 M⊙ and circumgalactic medium metallicity measurements from 11 studies of local and high-redshift galaxies, spanning four orders of magnitude in luminosity and eight orders of magnitude in mass. In agreement with previous studies, we find that the L-Z relation for compact galaxies is not universal, but instead depends on luminosity, with the faintest galaxies exhibiting the highest metallicities. However, we find that the M-Z relation is universal, independent of mass, and that this relation holds over an order of magnitude longer than previously reported, from the Milky Way to dwarf galaxies a factor of ~100 times less massive. We show that this lack of evolution in the M-Z relation implies that the star-formation histories and chemical enrichment histories of these galaxies must be closely coupled over nearly all of their lifetimes. Using stellar population models, we demonstrate that this coupling can be achieved if the duration of star formation is proportional to the gas mass of the galaxy and if the gas is mixed well with the stars at all times.

We present a method for unsupervised learning of foreground object detection, based on clustering and density estimation. It consists in the training of two components: a classifier that assigns to each pixel a label corresponding to the cluster to which the foreground object belongs, and a density estimator that models the background. The labels are determined during training by a clustering procedure that identifies the regions of the image dominated by the foreground objects. The resulting method is effective in detecting the foreground objects in a fully unsupervised manner. We demonstrate the performance of the method on a synthetic dataset and on a difficult real-world dataset of people in crowded scenes.

 Our method is related to the popular density-based clustering methods

Recent progress in convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture design has propelled the advancement of semantic segmentation, especially in the context of natural image datasets. However, the assumption that the training data is abundantly labeled, which is often satisfied in natural image segmentation, does not hold for specialized domains such as food image segmentation, which demands much effort and expense to collect and label. To overcome the lack of labeled training data, we can utilize the prior knowledge in the form of rules or culinary knowledge to learn a segmentation model. In this work, we borrow ideas from the recent advancement in the field of salient object detection and propose a saliency-aware class-agnostic segmentation approach for food images. Specifically, we first utilize a pre-trained CNN as a feature encoder to extract mid-level features and then build a segmentation model that is trained by explicitly incorporating the prior knowledge of food images, which is in the form of a global saliency map. The global saliency map is learned in a class-agnostic manner, but is tailored to the food domain.

Recent advances in neuroimaging acquisition enabled large-scale recordings of neural activity in many regions across the entire human brain at increasing resolution. While the field of connectomics aimed to map the intricate patterns of fiber connections across the entire brain, current state-of-the-art algorithms for reconstructing fiber tracts from diffusion MRI (dMRI) images are far from delivering feasible runtime performance for mapping ultra-large scale datasets, which typically consist of several thousands of images with each image requiring several minutes of computational processing. In this paper, we present a deep learning based approach that aims to accelerate the reconstruction process of fiber connections across the human brain. We exploit recent advances in image segmentation through structured loss functions that promote the reconstruction of anatomically meaningful segments while retaining the advantage of end-to-end differentiability. We train our deep learning architecture on large-scale datasets of simulated as well as real dMRI images. In contrast to related work, we provide a thorough evaluation of the algorithm's performance by comparing it to state-of-the-art methods on real datasets.

Recent developments in imaging medicine have led to a significant increase in the size of 3D medical images, posing a great challenge for efficient transmission, storage and segmentation in the clouds. In this paper, we propose a machine vision guided 3D medical image compression approach to address this issue. Our method leverages the power of deep learning to learn a compression model directly from the images, which is trained using a large number of images collected from clinical studies. The compression model is designed to take into account the specific characteristics of medical images, such as their typically low entropy and the need for precise segmentation. We evaluate our method on a large dataset of real clinical images and demonstrate that it achieves a significant reduction in the file size while maintaining high quality and enabling accurate segmentation in the clouds. Our method can be seamlessly integrated into the existing workflow of medical imaging and has the potential to significantly reduce the storage and transmission costs of 3D medical images.

Deep learning is a promising method for tongue surface tracking from real-time ultrasound videos. We present a simple yet effective method to train a deep neural network for tongue surface detection. Unlike most previous methods that trace the contour of the tongue, our method detects the landmarks on the tongue surface. It is more robust to the ambiguous contour around the tongue border in ultrasound videos, and it is more efficient in terms of computation and training data. We evaluated our method on real-time ultrasound videos, and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

 Our tongue surface detection network is based on a modified version of the popular Faster R-CNN [1] with additional novel improvements.

Recent developments in neural network architecture have boosted the performance of image segmentation. In this paper, we propose FusionNet, a deep fully residual convolutional neural network for image segmentation in connectomics. FusionNet incorporates several techniques that have been shown to be effective in image segmentation, including an atrous convolutional layer, a residual block, and a dense connection pattern. We evaluate FusionNet on the task of segmentation of neuronal structures in connectomic images, and show that it outperforms existing state-of-the-art models. In particular, when applied to segmenting neurons in mouse cortical tissue, FusionNet achieves a precision of 94.3% and recall of 92.6% on cell bodies, and 85.5% precision and 88.4% recall on axon initial segments. Code is available at https://github.com/andy-connectome/FusionNet.

Nature-inspired algorithms perform well in image segmentation, but the choice of a base algorithm has a significant impact on performance. In this research, the application of four nature-inspired algorithms (particle swarm optimization, bacterial foraging optimization, cuckoo search, and firefly algorithm) for multi-threshold image segmentation is compared. Metrics including computation time and segmentation quality are considered. The results show that the firefly algorithm outperforms the others in both metrics. Particle swarm optimization achieved the second best performance. Cuckoo search and bacterial foraging optimization did not perform as well as the top two algorithms.

We give an introduction to stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). After recalling the definition and properties of classical Gaussian SPDEs, we discuss existence and uniqueness results for general nonlinear SPDEs in a Gaussian setting. We then turn to a class of nonlinear SPDEs in the Gaussian setting which possess a unique solution and focus on the question of obtaining a probabilistic representation for the solution in terms of a stochastic flow of maps. Here the underlying stochastic flow is solution to a stochastic differential equation with a countable number of Brownian drivers. We present a general approach for obtaining such a representation under mild conditions on the coefficients of the SPDE. 

 As a concrete example, we consider a class of nonlinear SPDEs that are associated to a stochastic flow of maps that is generated by a stochastic differential equation with a countable number of Brownian drivers.

We provide analytic expressions for the stochastic distance between two relaxed complex Wishart distributions, under various metrics such as the Hellinger distance, the total variation distance, and the Kantorovich metric. These results are useful for comparing the distributions of relaxed complex Wishart variables, which are commonly used in statistical modeling and machine learning. The expressions are straightforward to implement and provide a robust and efficient alternative to existing simulation-based approaches. We illustrate the use of our results with a example comparing the distributions of relaxed complex Wishart variables under two different covariance models.

 ```

Wishart distributions are commonly used in statistical modeling and machine learning, particularly for modeling the distribution of random matrices. In many applications, it is important to compare the distributions of relaxed complex Wishart variables, which are obtained by adding a small amount of noise to the variables.

Medical image segmentation is important in medicine yet suffers from human error introduced during manual labeling. A significant challenge in training deep learning models for segmentation is the amount of ground truth (GT) required, which is time-consuming and expensive to generate. As a result, there has been increasing interest in using synthetic data for training. However, the quality of the GT in synthetic data is typically superior to that in real data, leading to the risk of overfitting. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to address both problems: the small amount of real GT and the error in the GT. We first use a U-Net deep learning architecture to segment images and then use a multi-scale graph cuts algorithm to refine the segmentation results.

We present an efficient and accurate approach for colorectal tumor segmentation based on 3D U-Net. Our method extends the 2D U-Net architecture to include 3D pooling and striding operations, enabling the network to effectively capture spatial dependencies and contextual information in volumetric data. To enhance performance, we introduce a region-of-interest (RoI) pooling layer that allows the network to focus on the most relevant tumor regions. Furthermore, we propose a 3D RoI-aware loss function that guides the network to learn more effectively from sparse ground truth labels. Our method demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on the benchmark CSI-MR colon tumor segmentation dataset, with a dice coefficient of 0.8218 and a sensitivity of 0.7383. In terms of efficiency, our approach achieves a speed of ~40 ms per case on a standard GPU, making it suitable for real-time or batch processing of large datasets.

Recent advances in deep neural networks have achieved significant performance in biomedical image segmentation. However, these models are data-hungry and require a large amount of labeled examples for training, which are difficult to obtain in the biomedical field due to the high cost of expert annotation. In this paper, we propose a universal decoding method, called Cascade Decoder, for training data-efficient segmentation models that can be applied to any image domain with only a few annotated examples. Cascade Decoder first utilizes a set of pre-trained decoders to extract features from the input image, and then learns a new decoder to refine the predictions based on the segmented images and their annotations. By cascading the decoders in a coarse-to-fine fashion, our method can effectively leverage both the global and local information in the image to achieve segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on three different image segmentation tasks: tumor cell segmentation from confocal images, neuron segmentation from electron microscopic images, and white matter fiber tract segmentation from T1-weighted MRI images, with only 10%, 4% and 0.5% of the images in the training set, respectively.

The dynamics of electrons in semiconductors is a fundamental issue that has been the subject of numerous studies. In this paper, we present a new approach to studying the dynamics of electrons in crystalline semiconductors. This approach is based on the solution of the Schrödinger equation for the electron wave function. The solution of this equation is found to be in good agreement with the results of experimental studies of the dynamics of electrons in crystalline semiconductors. We also compare our results with the results of other approaches to the study of electron dynamics in semiconductors. In addition, we examine the effects of various factors on the dynamics of electrons in these materials.

We present a graph-based framework for natural image segmentation based on affinity fusion. Our approach leverages the multi-scale graph structure to capture the image context and fuse the multi-scale segmentation results. By iteratively refining the graph representation and updating the segmentation, our algorithm effectively combines both global and local information for accurate segmentation. We introduce a novel affinity learning scheme to adaptively estimate the affinity matrix, which measures the similarity between pixels. The proposed method is fully automatic, parameter-free, and is able to handle any image size. We evaluate our approach on the VOC 2012 segmentation benchmark and achieve competitive results compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

Line patterns are very common in images. They appear, for example, in aerial and satellite images, temperature maps, brightness temperature maps, and many other types of images. The problem of line pattern delineation, i.e., segmenting a line pattern into individual lines, is therefore of practical importance. In this paper we propose a new approach to line pattern delineation based on the use of B-COSFIRE filters. These filters have good frequency response characteristics and are straightforward to implement. In addition, a new gradient-based line selector is proposed.

Multi-channel image segmentation is a classical problem in image processing, with many applications in areas such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and video processing. In this paper, we propose a new approach to multi-channel image segmentation based on component trees. Our method utilizes the derivative information of the image channels to build a hierarchy of segments, which can be recursively split into smaller segments. The proposed method is simple to implement and efficient to compute, and it can handle images with different numbers of channels. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on a number of challenging segmentation problems, including a remotely sensed image dataset and a multi-channel medical imaging dataset. Our results show that the proposed method can achieve accurate segmentation results and is competitive with state-of-the-art methods.

Two-dimensional (2D) materials offer a unique opportunity to combine different atoms in a single van der Waals heterostructure, with atomic precision, to create engineered meta-materials with unprecedented electrical, optical, and magnetic properties. One of the current challenges is the lack of understanding of the fundamental dielectric properties of these meta-materials and how they originate from the properties of the constituting 2D materials. Here, we present a first principles theory to calculate the dielectric function of a van der Waals heterostructure made up of two different 2D materials. We show how the fundamental dielectric response is influenced by the properties of the individual layers, such as the atomic structure, the electronic states, and the optical transitions. As an example, we calculate the dielectric functions of van der Waals heterostructures made up of h-BN and graphene, and we show that the fundamental dielectric response is influenced by both the intralayer and the interlayer physics, which include resonant states in both regions and a strong interlayer coupling. The results agree well with recent measurements.

Semantic image segmentation, which aims to assign semantic labels to every pixel in an image, is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Recent progresses in this field are mainly driven by deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks (CNNs). However, directly applying CNNs on the pixel level prediction is computationally expensive, and the network architecture is difficult to extend to segment complex scenes. In this paper, we present a progressively diffused network (PDNet) for semantic image segmentation. PDNet employs a regional feature aggregation scheme to hierarchically refine the segmentation results and effectively capture long-range dependencies in an image. A diffused structure is introduced to model the spatial variations of the image, which enables the network to focus on difficult regions and avoid unnecessary computations on easy regions.

Medical image segmentation is a fundamental preliminary step for computed tomography (CT) images towards computerized tumor diagnosis and therapy planning. Recently, deep learning based on fully convolutional networks (FCNs) has produced significant advancements in medical image segmentation. However, directly applying FCNs to segment CT images is challenging due to the substantial variability of tumor appearance, the presence of similar structures, and the reduced amount of manually annotated training data. In this paper, we propose a novel mixed-supervised dual-network (MSDN) for automatic CT image segmentation. Given the scarce amount of manually annotated data, our MSDN further utilizes a large set of automatically segmented images, which is obtained by a fully supervised deep learning algorithm, as additional weakly labeled training data. We employ a dual-network architecture, where the prior network is trained in a fully supervised manner, and the latter network is trained with both the fully supervised and weak supervision.

Recent advances in deep learning have achieved great performance in medical image segmentation. However, deep learning methods usually ignore the observer variation, which may lead to inconsistent segmentation results among different observers. In this paper, we present a new framework to achieve observer- variation aware medical image segmentation, which combines deep learning and surrogate-assisted genetic algorithms. Given the segmented images from multiple observers, our framework learns a deep neural network in a data-driven manner to capture the common patterns for segmentation, while genetic algorithms are used to optimize the segmentation protocols to achieve better segmentation consistency across observers. We apply our method to segment lumbar vertebrae in CT images. Experimental results show the effectiveness of our method in improving the segmentation consistency.

We reexamine the recently proposed Atrous Convolution (AC) for semantic image segmentation. Despite its popularity, we show that the performance of AC deteriorates as the average stride length in the encoder increases, which is crucial for preserving spatial information and resisting overfitting. Through analysis and experiments, we find that this limitation arises from the sharing of the atrous rate among different convolutional layers, which restricts the adaptability of the atrous rate to feature hierarchies. To address this problem, we propose a simple yet effective method called Adaptive Atrous Rate (AAR), which adaptively estimates the atrous rate for each layer. AAR not only improves the segmentation performance but also significantly reduces the memory usage and accelerates the training process. We implement the state-of-the-art segmentation models with AAR and demonstrate its advantage over the models with the original AC on multiple datasets, including Cityscapes and ACDC.

We study interference between two single photons and two-photon spontaneous superposition using a polarization-based quantum eraser setup. The two-photon state is produced by an spontaneous parametric down-conversion photon pair source, and the photons are sent through a polarization beam splitter, with one arm containing a quantum eraser and the other a half-wave plate, which can be used to change the polarization of a photon. The two photons are then measured using two polarization-sensitive detectors. We find that when the half-wave plate is not set to a special angle, the two-photon coincidence rate shows an interference pattern, with maxima and minima corresponding to the two different polarization settings of the quantum eraser. However, when the half-wave plate is set to a special angle, we observe that the two-photon coincidence rate is always at its maximum, independent of the polarization setting of the quantum eraser. This demonstrates a breakdown of the spontaneous superposition of the two-photon state, and is explained by a simple classical model.

Patterns are ubiquitous in natural language texts, formal languages, and biological sequences. Furthermore, patterns can often be embedded within one another forming hierarchical structures. For example, in a natural language sentence, individual words can form phrases, and phrases can form clauses, etc. Similarly, in genetic sequences, motifs (short patterns) can form larger structures such as genes, which in turn form chromosomes. These hierarchical structures can be represented as nodes in a tree, where each node has potentially multiple parent nodes and multiple child nodes. Such tree structures are referred to as tree patterns.

A long-running webcam installed in 2007 at Lake Mendota, Wisconsin, has provided an opportunity to develop a time series of lake ice coverage and thaw dates. Comparing webcam images with those from crowd-sourced volunteers using the same web interface shows that citizen scientists can provide useful data, but with considerable variability. Guidance for volunteers on how to interpret webcam images of lake ice leads to more accurate and precise measurements, but variability in measurements persists. Crowd-sourced data, if applied to a large region with adequate volunteer training, could provide a valuable supplement to satellite data for monitoring lake ice cover. However, automated analysis of webcam images, as developed here, provides the most accurate and precise data. The webcam-based time series reveals a significant shift toward later ice coverage in fall and earlier ice-out dates in spring over the 13-year record.

We show that linear dispersive filtering near atomic resonance can lead to time-reversal of light. In particular, near the 1183 nm resonance in Xenon, a 1 nm thin layer of the gas achieves almost perfect time-reversal of the transmitted light. We find excellent agreement between numerical solutions of Maxwell's equations and experimental measurements. Our results open new possibilities for time-reversal of light using readily available materials, with potential applications in optical imaging and communication. 

 We further show that a thin layer of any linear material, regardless of its atomic or molecular composition, can be used to reverse the group velocity of light. Finally, we discuss the limitations of our experimental approach, and outline future directions.

Recent progress in deep learning allows training models to learn image segmentation from labeled images, but training data with ground truth is often not available in practice. Unsupervised learning offers a appealing alternative but learning meaningful representations of images without guidance remains challenging. In this paper, we exploit differentiable kernel clustering as a building block for learning an effective image representation without any labels. Our method clusters image patches in a way that captures local structures and, at the same time, is differentiable with respect to the inputs. This property enables training by minimizing an appropriate energy function on a graph, which is defined by the image gradients. We show that the resulting algorithm is capable of simultaneously clustering image patches and segmenting the image in a supervised manner, given only the image itself as input.

Abstract:

Deep learning (DL) has recently emerged as a powerful tool for machine health monitoring (MHM). In this survey, we provide an overview of the current state of the art in DL for MHM, including key research challenges, opportunities, and limitations. We begin by introducing the basic concepts of DL and MHM, and then review the different ways in which DL has been applied to MHM, including fault detection, diagnosis, and prognosis. We then discuss the advantages and limitations of DL for MHM, and highlight key research challenges such as data acquisition, model selection, and deployment. Finally, we provide a brief overview of the current state of the art in DL for MHM, and highlight potential research directions. We hope that this survey will provide a comprehensive and informative overview of the current state of the art in DL for MHM, and inspire further research and development in this exciting field.

Arxiv abstract:
 We present a novel semi-supervised learning framework for few-shot medical image segmentation, which we refer to as PoissonSeg. In medical image analysis, acquiring manually annotated images for training can be expensive, and transferring pre-trained models to new sites and modalities is challenging. To tackle these problems, we exploit a recently proposed poisson learning framework, which enables us to leverage abundant unlabeled data and prior knowledge, and develop a new framework that is suitable for few-shot learning. In our method, we minimize a poisson loss that enforces the agreement between segmentations and the prior knowledge, and a segmentation difference loss that encourages the agreement between predictions and a few labeled images. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on three different abdominal image segmentation benchmarks, and show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches for few-shot learning.

Articular cartilage plays an essential role in the functioning of joints, as it allows for smooth articulation and dissipation of loads. However, it is highly susceptible to injury and degradation, particularly in the presence of repetitive loading. In this research paper, a comprehensive finite element model is presented to investigate the effects of cyclic loading on articular cartilage lesion formation. The model incorporates the material properties and morphology of articular cartilage, allowing for a realistic representation of the tissue's behavior.

 The results of the simulation show that cyclic loading significantly contributes to the formation of articular cartilage lesions. The model was able to capture the progression of damage in the cartilage tissue, highlighting the regions of highest stress and strain that were susceptible to injury.

Chilies are one of the most important cash crops in Mexico and it is the second most important vegetable after the tomato. Time consuming and tedious manual inspection is currently done in agriculture to estimate the percentage of defects in the harvested produce. Defect inspection is needed for proper grading and to determine if the produce meets the stringent quality requirements of the exporter. This work focuses on defect segmentation of chili pepper X-ray images. Successful segmentation was achieved using a texture based approach. A Gabor filter is used as a texture descriptor.

Deepfake refers to the phenomenon of maliciously manipulating multimedia contents, especially image and video data, using artificial intelligence techniques to impersonate a person doing or saying something they never did or said. Detecting deepfake contents is of paramount importance to uphold the integrity of media communication. In this paper, we focus on detecting forged facial expressions in still images, which is a fundamental yet challenging task. We propose a novel approach to detect forged facial expressions using a separable convolutional neural network (SCNN) and image segmentation. Our approach first extracts a compact feature vector from the input image using a deep convolutional neural network (DCNN). Then, we apply image segmentation to extract the regions of interest (ROIs) from the input image.

We present a fast constraint propagation algorithm for image segmentation based on label fusion of watershed segments. The approach is motivated by the shape prior of watershed segments, which reflects the local connectivity of the image pixels. The proposed algorithm efficiently computes a score for each pixel based on the constraints from the watershed segmentation and fuses the scores of neighboring segments to obtain the final segmentation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach on a variety of images, and show that it produces a segmentation that is more accurate and coherent compared to existing algorithms. The proposed algorithm is fast enough to be used in real-time applications.
```
