The proposed method involves the use of strided convolutions, which allow for the efficient processing of large-scale images while maintaining a high level of detail. The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the performance of strided tensor networks in comparison to traditional image segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research opens up new avenues for the application of tensor networks in computer vision and image processing tasks.

This paper presents a novel single chain slip-spring model for fast rheology simulations of entangled polymers on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). The model is designed to overcome the computational challenges associated with the simulation of entangled polymers, which are critical in understanding their rheological properties. The model leverages the parallel processing capabilities of GPUs to significantly reduce the computational time. The paper provides a detailed description of the model, its implementation on GPUs, and its validation against experimental data. The results demonstrate that the model can accurately predict the rheological behavior of entangled polymers and can perform simulations several times faster than traditional CPU-based methods. This work opens up new possibilities for the study of complex polymer systems and their applications in various industries.

This paper presents a novel approach to unsupervised image segmentation, termed as Deep Superpixel Cut (DSC). The DSC method leverages the strengths of deep learning and superpixel algorithms to achieve high-quality segmentation results. The proposed method first generates superpixels from the input image, then uses a deep neural network to learn the features of each superpixel. These features are then used to construct a graph, where each superpixel is a node and the edges represent the similarity between superpixels. A graph cut algorithm is then applied to segment the image. The DSC method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, termed Maximin Affinity Learning. The method is based on the principle of maximizing the minimum affinity of any two adjacent segments in an image. The proposed algorithm learns a segmentation function from a set of training images with corresponding ground truth segmentations. The function is then used to segment new images. The paper provides a detailed description of the algorithm, its implementation, and its performance on several benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate that the Maximin Affinity Learning method outperforms existing state-of-the-art image segmentation techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper investigates the influence of ground truth annotation quality on the performance of semantic image segmentation in the context of traffic conditions. The study employs various image datasets with different levels of annotation quality to train and test semantic segmentation models. The results demonstrate a significant correlation between the quality of ground truth annotations and the performance of the models. High-quality annotations lead to improved model accuracy and efficiency in identifying and categorizing different traffic conditions. The findings underscore the importance of accurate and detailed ground truth annotations in the development of robust and reliable semantic image segmentation models for traffic condition monitoring and prediction. This research provides valuable insights for the advancement of computer vision applications in traffic management and autonomous driving systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using sparse subset selection. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by selecting a sparse subset of pixels that best represent the entire image. This is achieved through a mathematical model that optimizes the selection of pixels based on their features and spatial relationships. The model is designed to handle large-scale images and is robust to variations in image quality and content. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing image segmentation techniques in terms of both segmentation quality and computational efficiency. The proposed approach has potential applications in various fields including computer vision, image processing, and machine learning.

This paper presents a novel mixed-supervised dual-network (MSDN) for medical image segmentation. The proposed model leverages both supervised and unsupervised learning methods to enhance the segmentation performance. The dual-network architecture consists of two interconnected networks: a supervised network trained with labeled data and an unsupervised network trained with unlabeled data. The two networks mutually reinforce each other during the training process, leading to improved segmentation accuracy. The effectiveness of the MSDN is evaluated on several medical imaging datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing segmentation methods. This research provides a new perspective on integrating supervised and unsupervised learning for medical image segmentation, potentially improving the efficiency and accuracy of disease diagnosis.

This paper presents a novel method for automatically segmenting the left atrium from cardiac images using successive 3D U-Nets and a contour loss. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of left atrium segmentation, which is crucial for diagnosing and treating various heart diseases. The method involves training two successive 3D U-Nets, with the first one focusing on the overall shape of the left atrium and the second one refining the details. A contour loss is also introduced to further enhance the segmentation accuracy by emphasizing the importance of the atrial boundary. Experimental results on a public dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for the development of automated cardiac image analysis tools.

This paper presents a novel 3D Coarse-to-Fine (C2F) framework for volumetric medical image segmentation. The proposed method aims to address the challenges of high computational cost and lack of accuracy in existing segmentation techniques. The C2F framework employs a two-stage process: a coarse segmentation stage that quickly identifies regions of interest, followed by a fine segmentation stage that refines these regions with high precision. The framework is designed to be adaptable to various types of medical imaging modalities and demonstrates superior performance in terms of accuracy and efficiency when compared to state-of-the-art methods. Experimental results on multiple public medical datasets confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework. This research has significant implications for improving diagnostic accuracy and treatment planning in healthcare.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using Convolutional Conditional Random Fields (Conv-CRFs). The proposed method leverages the strengths of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and conditional random fields (CRFs) to achieve high-quality segmentation results. The Conv-CRF model is designed to capture long-range spatial dependencies in images, which are often overlooked by traditional CNNs. The model is trained end-to-end, allowing for seamless integration with existing deep learning architectures. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy. The paper also provides insights into the workings of Conv-CRFs, shedding light on their potential for a wide range of image analysis tasks.

This paper investigates the interaction of $F(R,T)$ gravity with modified Chaplygin gas in the context of cosmology. The $F(R,T)$ gravity model, where R represents the Ricci scalar and T the trace of the energy-momentum tensor, is considered as an alternative to dark energy for explaining the accelerated expansion of the universe. The modified Chaplygin gas is a model that unifies dark matter and dark energy. We derive the field equations and study their solutions, focusing on the evolution of the scale factor and the deceleration parameter. We also analyze the stability of the solutions and the behavior of the equation of state parameter. Our results show that the interaction between $F(R,T)$ gravity and modified Chaplygin gas can lead to a viable cosmological model that is consistent with observational data.

This paper presents a novel approach to joint image segmentation and shape matching, leveraging the concept of Wasserstein modes. The proposed method aims to achieve global optimality, a significant improvement over existing techniques that often settle for local optima. The approach is based on the mathematical theory of optimal transport, specifically the Wasserstein distance, which provides a robust measure of dissimilarity between shapes. The paper introduces the concept of Wasserstein modes, which are used to capture the dominant modes of shape variability in a given dataset. The proposed method is tested on various datasets and demonstrates superior performance in terms of accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods. The results suggest that the Wasserstein modes-based approach holds great promise for various applications in computer vision and medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to parametric image segmentation of humans using structural shape priors. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of human image segmentation, a critical task in computer vision. The proposed method incorporates structural shape priors, which provide a probabilistic model of the human shape, into the segmentation process. This approach allows for more accurate segmentation by considering the inherent structure and variability of the human shape. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The findings of this study have significant implications for various applications, including video surveillance, human-computer interaction, and medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to portrait segmentation using a boundary-sensitive network. The proposed method aims to address the common issue of inaccurate boundary detection in existing segmentation models. The boundary-sensitive network incorporates a new loss function that emphasizes boundary pixels, improving the accuracy of boundary detection. The network also utilizes a multi-scale architecture to capture both global and local features of the portrait. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art portrait segmentation techniques in terms of both boundary accuracy and overall segmentation performance. This research has significant implications for applications such as image editing, virtual reality, and augmented reality.

This paper presents a novel evaluation criterion for ultra-high resolution cell membrane segmentation based on human perception. The study aims to bridge the gap between traditional evaluation metrics and human visual perception, which is crucial in the field of biological image analysis. The proposed criterion incorporates the human visual system's characteristics and the specific task requirements of cell membrane segmentation. The paper also introduces a new dataset of ultra-high resolution images with human-annotated ground truth for benchmarking. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed criterion aligns more closely with human perception compared to traditional metrics, providing a more accurate and reliable evaluation of cell membrane segmentation algorithms. This research has significant implications for the development and assessment of image segmentation techniques in biological and medical imaging.

This paper presents an in-depth analysis of optical quasar polarization vectors on a large scale. The study utilizes a comprehensive dataset of quasar polarization measurements, revealing a significant pattern in the alignment of these vectors. The findings suggest that the orientation of quasar polarization vectors is not random, as previously assumed, but exhibits a coherent orientation over a large scale. This unexpected alignment could potentially challenge the standard cosmological principle, which assumes isotropy and homogeneity of the universe. The paper further discusses the possible cosmological implications and potential sources of systematic errors that could produce such a pattern. The results of this study open up new avenues for understanding the large-scale structure of the universe and the fundamental physics of quasars.

This paper presents a comprehensive performance analysis of linear-equality-constrained least-squares estimation. The study focuses on the efficiency, accuracy, and computational complexity of this estimation method in various scenarios. The paper begins with a detailed introduction to the mathematical principles underlying the method, followed by a discussion on its potential applications. The main body of the paper presents a series of experiments designed to evaluate the performance of the method under different conditions. The results indicate that the linear-equality-constrained least-squares estimation method provides reliable and accurate results, with a reasonable computational cost. The paper concludes with a discussion on potential improvements and future research directions.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the solutions to the T-systems with principal coefficients. The T-systems, a class of discrete integrable systems, have been extensively studied due to their wide applications in mathematical physics, combinatorics, and representation theory. However, the solutions to these systems with principal coefficients have remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach to solve these systems, leveraging the properties of the principal coefficients. We also provide a detailed analysis of the solutions' behavior under different conditions. The results not only enrich the theory of T-systems but also open up new avenues for further research in the field of discrete integrable systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on generalized trees, a fundamental concept in various fields such as computer science, mathematics, and data analysis. The paper primarily focuses on the algebraic and logical descriptions of these structures. It begins with an introduction to generalized trees, followed by an in-depth exploration of their algebraic properties. The paper then delves into the logical descriptions, highlighting the role of logic in understanding and manipulating these structures. The study also provides a comparative analysis of the algebraic and logical approaches, elucidating their interconnections and differences. The findings of this research contribute to the theoretical understanding of generalized trees and offer valuable insights for practical applications in areas such as algorithm design, database theory, and artificial intelligence.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using volume preserving optimal transport with entropic regularization. The proposed method aims to address the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques, which often fail to preserve the volume of the segmented regions. The entropic regularization optimal transport (EROT) model is introduced, which not only ensures volume preservation but also improves the computational efficiency. The paper further explores the application of this model in deep learning, demonstrating its effectiveness in tasks such as object detection and image classification. Experimental results on various datasets confirm the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational speed. This research opens up new avenues for enhancing image segmentation techniques and their applications in deep learning.

This paper presents a novel approach to model selection for time series data using the Graphical Lasso (GLasso) method. The primary focus is on the application of GLasso for estimating sparse inverse covariance matrices, which are crucial in understanding the underlying dependency structure of multivariate time series. The paper introduces a new criterion for model selection, which is based on the stability of the estimated network structure over different time points. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive simulations and real data analysis. The results show that the GLasso-based model selection method outperforms traditional methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research provides a new perspective on model selection for time series data and opens up new avenues for further research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving the self-repelling snake model using the Split Bregman algorithm. The self-repelling snake model is a complex mathematical model used in image processing and computer vision, particularly in edge detection and object tracking. Traditional methods of solving this model are computationally intensive and often result in suboptimal solutions. The Split Bregman algorithm, a fast and efficient iterative method, is proposed as a solution to these challenges. The paper provides a detailed explanation of the algorithm, its implementation, and its advantages over existing methods. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the Split Bregman algorithm in solving the self-repelling snake model, highlighting its potential for use in real-time image processing applications.

This paper introduces SimPropNet, an innovative approach to few-shot image segmentation that enhances similarity propagation. The study addresses the limitations of current methods, which often struggle with complex segmentation tasks due to the lack of sufficient annotated data. SimPropNet leverages a novel similarity propagation mechanism that effectively captures the inherent relationship between support and query images. It also incorporates a dual-attention module to refine the propagated similarity. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that SimPropNet significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. The results suggest that the proposed method has great potential for practical applications in image segmentation tasks with limited annotated data.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on dynamic spatial autoregressive models with autoregressive and heteroskedastic disturbances. The research focuses on the development and analysis of a new class of models that incorporate both spatial and temporal dependencies, along with heteroskedasticity in the error terms. The paper provides a detailed theoretical framework, including the derivation of the maximum likelihood estimators and their asymptotic properties. It also discusses the implementation of these models using a Bayesian approach. The performance of the proposed models is evaluated through a series of simulation studies and real data applications. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed models in capturing complex spatial and temporal dynamics, and their superiority over existing models in terms of predictive accuracy.

This paper presents an in-depth analysis of sparse dictionaries for online learning with kernels. The study focuses on the application of kernel methods in online learning, particularly in the context of sparse dictionary learning. The paper introduces a novel algorithm that combines the advantages of kernel methods and sparse dictionary learning, providing a more efficient and effective solution for online learning tasks. The proposed method is evaluated through various experiments, demonstrating its superior performance in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The results suggest that the integration of kernel methods and sparse dictionary learning can significantly improve the performance of online learning systems. The paper also discusses potential future research directions in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to liver segmentation in abdominal CT images using an auto-context neural network and self-supervised contour attention. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of liver segmentation, a critical step in diagnosing and treating liver diseases. The proposed method integrates the auto-context algorithm into a deep learning framework to capture contextual information and enhance the segmentation performance. Additionally, a self-supervised contour attention mechanism is introduced to focus on challenging boundary areas. Experimental results on public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and has potential applications in clinical practice for liver disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to disease classification and segmentation using interpretability-driven sample selection and self-supervised learning. The study aims to improve the interpretability and performance of deep learning models in medical imaging. The proposed method leverages self-supervised learning to select informative samples and uses them to train a disease classification and segmentation model. The model's interpretability is enhanced by visualizing the learned features and decision-making process. Experimental results on several medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the interpretability and accuracy of disease classification and segmentation. The study also discusses potential applications and future directions for further research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to deformable multi-scale image registration, known as test-time training. This method addresses the challenge of registering images that differ significantly in appearance due to changes in scale, orientation, and deformation. The proposed approach leverages the power of deep learning to train a registration model at test time, using only the pair of images to be registered. This allows the model to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input images, improving registration accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that test-time training outperforms traditional registration methods on several benchmark datasets, providing more accurate and robust results across a wide range of image transformations. The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in medical imaging, remote sensing, and computer vision.

This paper presents a novel approach to sparse recovery in multi-sensor measurement systems. The study focuses on the optimization of sparse recovery algorithms, which are crucial for accurate and efficient data acquisition in various fields such as signal processing, computer vision, and machine learning. The proposed method leverages the inherent sparsity in multi-sensor measurements to improve the recovery of original signals from underdetermined linear systems. The paper provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis, demonstrating the superiority of the proposed method over existing sparse recovery techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is further validated through extensive simulations and real-world experiments. The results indicate that the proposed method significantly enhances the accuracy and efficiency of sparse recovery in multi-sensor measurement systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to interactive binary image segmentation with a focus on edge preservation. The proposed method combines user interaction and advanced algorithms to accurately segment images while preserving the integrity of edges. The technique is based on graph cuts and active contours, which are optimized to handle binary images. The paper also introduces a new edge-preserving smoothing filter that enhances the segmentation results. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and edge preservation. This research has significant implications for various applications, including medical imaging, computer vision, and digital image processing.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on path checking for Metric Temporal Logic (MTL) and Timed Propositional Temporal Logic (TPTL) over data words. Data words are sequences of data values from an infinite domain, annotated with time stamps, and are used to model timed and data-intensive systems. The paper introduces a novel algorithm for path checking, which is proven to be highly efficient and effective. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using a variety of benchmarks, demonstrating its potential for practical applications. The paper also provides a detailed comparison of MTL and TPTL, highlighting their respective strengths and weaknesses in handling data words. The findings of this study contribute to the understanding of temporal logic over data words and offer valuable insights for future research in this area.

This paper introduces MixSearch, a novel approach to search for domain-generalized medical image segmentation architectures. The proposed method leverages a mixed search space and a multi-objective search algorithm to discover architectures that can generalize across different medical imaging domains. MixSearch is designed to address the challenges of domain shift and data scarcity in medical image analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that the architectures found by MixSearch outperform existing state-of-the-art methods on several medical image segmentation benchmarks. Furthermore, the discovered architectures exhibit strong domain generalization capabilities, achieving high performance across different imaging modalities and anatomical structures. This research contributes to the advancement of automated machine learning (AutoML) techniques in the field of medical image analysis.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the development of a robust and generalized medical image segmentation framework. The proposed framework aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image analysis, which is crucial for diagnosis, treatment planning, and medical research. The paper discusses various techniques and methodologies used in image segmentation, including deep learning algorithms, and their application in the medical field. It also addresses the challenges faced in the implementation of these techniques, such as the need for large annotated datasets and the variability in medical images. The paper further proposes solutions to overcome these challenges, such as the use of transfer learning and data augmentation. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves the performance of medical image segmentation, making it a promising tool for clinical applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to gastric tumor segmentation using a patch-based reiterative learning method. The study addresses the challenge of partial labeling in medical imaging, where only a small portion of the images are labeled due to the time-consuming nature of the process. The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the segmentation performance. It involves a reiterative learning process that alternates between segmentation and re-labeling, gradually refining the segmentation results. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through extensive experiments on a gastric tumor dataset, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis, particularly in the context of gastric cancer diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to facial landmark detection and shape fitting using deep regression of shape model parameters. The proposed method leverages the power of deep learning to predict the parameters of a shape model in a super-realtime manner. The method is based on a convolutional neural network (CNN) that is trained to directly estimate the parameters of a statistical shape model from raw pixel intensities. The proposed approach outperforms existing methods in terms of speed and accuracy, achieving a significant improvement in facial landmark detection. The method is also robust to variations in pose, expression, and illumination. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on polynomial time algorithms for bi-criteria, multi-objective, and ratio problems in clustering and imaging. The focus is on normalized cut and ratio regions, which are critical in image segmentation and data clustering. The paper introduces novel algorithms that efficiently solve these problems, providing a significant improvement over existing methods. The algorithms are based on a rigorous mathematical framework and are proven to have polynomial time complexity. The paper also includes a detailed analysis of the performance of these algorithms, demonstrating their effectiveness and efficiency in various scenarios. This is the first part of a two-part series, with the second part focusing on other aspects of clustering and imaging problems.

This paper presents a novel approach to medical image segmentation using semi-supervised few-shot learning. The study aims to address the challenge of limited annotated medical images in the field of healthcare. The proposed method leverages both labeled and unlabeled data to improve the performance of segmentation tasks. The model is trained on a small number of labeled images (few-shot) and a large number of unlabeled images (semi-supervised). Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing few-shot learning methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research has significant implications for medical image analysis, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy and patient care.

This paper introduces LT-Net, a novel framework for one-shot medical image segmentation by learning reversible voxel-wise correspondence. The proposed method leverages label transfer to address the challenge of limited annotated medical images. LT-Net is designed to learn a dense correspondence between a pair of 3D volumes, which can be reversed to enable the transfer of manual labels from a source image to a target image. The model is trained on pairs of images with one being manually annotated, and the other being the target image. The effectiveness of LT-Net is evaluated on multiple public datasets, demonstrating superior performance in comparison to existing one-shot segmentation methods. The results suggest that LT-Net can effectively learn voxel-wise correspondence and facilitate accurate label transfer, providing a promising solution for one-shot medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to learning versatile neural architectures by propagating network codes. The study introduces a new method that uses a genetic algorithm to evolve network codes, which are then used to generate neural architectures. The proposed method is capable of learning a wide range of architectures, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs). The results demonstrate that the evolved architectures outperform manually designed architectures and other automated design methods on several benchmark datasets. The study also shows that the proposed method can effectively learn to propagate network codes, enabling the generation of versatile neural architectures. This research contributes to the field of automated machine learning, providing a new way to design neural networks that can adapt to different tasks and data types.

This paper presents a novel approach to semi-supervised learning for aggregated multilayer graphs using diffuse interface methods and fast matrix vector products. The study focuses on the challenges of learning from large-scale graph data, which is often high-dimensional and complex. The proposed method combines the diffuse interface model, which is effective in capturing the intrinsic geometric structure of data, with fast matrix vector products, which significantly reduce computational cost. The method is applied to semi-supervised learning tasks on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational speed. This research provides a new perspective and practical tools for semi-supervised learning on large-scale graph data.

This paper presents an in-depth study on the tracking of fast neutrons, particles that play a significant role in nuclear reactions. The research focuses on the development and application of advanced techniques and technologies for fast neutron detection and tracking. The paper discusses the challenges associated with fast neutron tracking, including their high penetration power and the difficulty in detecting them directly. It also explores various methods used in tracking fast neutrons, such as time-of-flight techniques, recoil proton techniques, and scintillation detectors. The paper further reviews the latest advancements in fast neutron tracking technology and discusses their potential applications in nuclear energy, medical imaging, and national security. The results of this study provide valuable insights for researchers and professionals in the field of nuclear physics and related disciplines.

This paper presents a novel approach to video segmentation using Recurrent Fully Convolutional Networks (RFCNs). The proposed method leverages the temporal continuity in videos, allowing for more accurate and efficient segmentation. The RFCNs are trained end-to-end, enabling the model to learn both spatial and temporal features. The proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art video segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also introduces a new dataset for video segmentation, providing a benchmark for future research in this area. The results demonstrate the potential of RFCNs for video segmentation and other video analysis tasks.

This paper provides a comprehensive historical survey of the proofs of Euclid's theorem on the infinitude of primes from its inception in 300 B.C. to the present day in 2022. The theorem, which asserts that there are infinitely many prime numbers, has been a cornerstone of number theory for over two millennia. This study traces the evolution of the theorem's proofs, highlighting the significant contributions of mathematicians across different eras and cultures. The paper also presents a novel proof of the theorem, contributing to the rich tapestry of mathematical thought surrounding this enduring proposition. The new proof is characterized by its simplicity and elegance, and it offers fresh insights into the nature of prime numbers. This paper is intended for both mathematicians interested in the history of their field and those seeking to understand the infinitude of primes from a new perspective.

This paper presents the Pyramid Medical Transformer (PMT), a novel approach for medical image segmentation. PMT leverages the transformer architecture, which has shown remarkable success in various fields, particularly in natural language processing. The proposed model introduces a pyramid structure to capture multi-scale features, which is crucial for medical image analysis. The PMT also incorporates a self-attention mechanism to focus on the most relevant features for segmentation. Extensive experiments on several medical image datasets demonstrate that the PMT outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. The results suggest that the transformer-based model holds great potential for medical image segmentation and other related tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, specifically for outlining in vitro cell colonies, using Principal Component Analysis (PCA). Traditional image segmentation techniques often struggle with the complexity and variability of cell colony images. Our method leverages the power of PCA to reduce the dimensionality of the image data, thereby simplifying the segmentation task. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a series of experiments on real-world cell colony images. The results show that our PCA-based method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for improving the automation of in vitro cell colony analysis, which is crucial for various biomedical applications.

This paper investigates the solutions of unit equations over finitely generated domains. The primary focus is on the effective results of these equations, which are integral to various fields of mathematics and computer science. The study employs a combination of algebraic and combinatorial methods to explore the structure and properties of these solutions. The results reveal a deep connection between the solutions of unit equations and the algebraic structure of finitely generated domains. The findings have significant implications for number theory, algebra, and computational mathematics. The paper also provides a comprehensive overview of the existing literature on unit equations, highlighting the gaps and potential areas for future research.

This paper presents a novel approach to segmenting several landmarks in running rodents using superpixels. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of rodent tracking in biomechanical and behavioral research. The proposed method involves the application of superpixels, a computer vision technique that groups pixels into perceptually meaningful atomic regions. This technique is used to segment the rodent's body parts, such as the head, body, and tail, in video frames. The results demonstrate that the superpixel-based method significantly outperforms traditional pixel-based methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of rodent tracking technologies and has potential applications in various fields, including neuroscience, ethology, and biomechanics.

This paper presents a novel approach to salient object detection in hyperspectral images using features learned from an unsupervised segmentation task. The study proposes a new method that leverages the rich spectral information in hyperspectral images and the power of unsupervised learning for feature extraction. The proposed method first performs an unsupervised segmentation task on the hyperspectral images to learn discriminative features. These features are then used to detect salient objects in the images. Experimental results on several hyperspectral image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting salient objects, outperforming several state-of-the-art methods. The study also discusses potential applications of the proposed method in various fields such as remote sensing, surveillance, and environmental monitoring.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of geometry in active learning for both binary and multi-class image segmentation. We propose a novel geometric approach that enhances the performance of active learning algorithms in image segmentation tasks. The paper discusses the theoretical aspects of the proposed method, followed by extensive experimental results on several benchmark datasets. The results demonstrate that the geometric approach significantly improves the segmentation accuracy compared to traditional active learning methods. Furthermore, the proposed method is shown to be effective for both binary and multi-class segmentation tasks, making it a versatile tool for various image analysis applications. The paper also provides insights into the role of geometry in active learning and its potential for further research in the field of image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to detect deepfake-forged contents using a separable convolutional neural network (SCNN) and image segmentation. Deepfake technology, which manipulates or fabricates visual content, poses significant threats to information credibility. Existing detection methods often fail to achieve satisfactory performance due to the high-quality synthesis of deepfakes. To address this issue, we propose a two-stage framework that first segments the facial region from the input image and then applies SCNN for deepfake detection. The SCNN is designed to capture both local and global features of the face, enhancing the discriminative power of the model. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to understanding pose variations within a shape population using constrained mixtures of factor analyzers. The study focuses on the challenge of modeling and learning the high-dimensional and non-linear variations in shape populations, particularly those caused by changes in pose. The proposed method employs a mixture of factor analyzers, which are constrained to capture pose-specific variations. The constraints are derived from a priori knowledge about the pose variations, making the model more interpretable and robust. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing pose variations, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for various applications, including computer vision, medical imaging, and machine learning.

This paper investigates the application of graph entropies in the field of texture segmentation of images. The study introduces a novel approach that utilizes graph entropy measures to extract texture features from images, which are then used for segmentation. The proposed method is based on the concept that texture can be represented as a complex network, where the nodes represent the pixels and the edges represent the spatial relationships between them. The entropy of this graph is then calculated to quantify the complexity of the texture. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional texture segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in various fields such as computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a novel approach to domain adaptation for medical image segmentation using margin preserving self-paced contrastive learning. The study addresses the challenge of domain shift, which often hampers the performance of deep learning models when applied to unseen data from different domains. The proposed method leverages the concept of self-paced learning and contrastive learning to learn more robust and domain-invariant features. It introduces a margin-preserving mechanism to enhance the discriminability of the learned representations. Extensive experiments on several medical image segmentation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, showing significant improvements over existing domain adaptation techniques. The results suggest that the proposed approach can effectively mitigate the domain shift problem, enhancing the generalizability of deep learning models for medical image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving fluid-structure interaction problems with thermal fluctuations using spatially adaptive stochastic multigrid methods. The proposed method is designed to handle the computational challenges posed by the multiscale nature of these problems, which involve complex interactions between fluid and solid domains under thermal fluctuations. The spatial adaptivity of the method allows for efficient resolution of local features, while the stochastic multigrid component provides a robust and scalable solver for the resulting discretized systems. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The results show significant improvements over traditional methods, particularly in scenarios with high thermal fluctuations. This research opens up new possibilities for the simulation of complex fluid-structure systems in various scientific and engineering applications.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of Neural Architecture Search (NAS) in the operational context of remote sensing. The research focuses on the use of NAS for automating the design of deep learning models, specifically for remote sensing image analysis. The paper provides a detailed case study, demonstrating the effectiveness of NAS in identifying optimal neural network architectures for complex remote sensing tasks. The results indicate that NAS can significantly improve the performance of remote sensing systems, while reducing the need for manual tuning of model parameters. The paper also discusses the challenges and potential solutions in implementing NAS in an operational context. This research contributes to the ongoing efforts to automate and optimize the application of deep learning in remote sensing.

This paper presents MobileNetV2, a novel architecture for mobile and embedded vision applications. The architecture is based on an inverted residual structure where the shortcut connections are between the thin bottleneck layers. The main building block of this architecture is a bottleneck depth-separable convolution with inverted residuals. The new architecture leads to significant improvements in both latency and accuracy over MobileNetV1. The paper also introduces two new features: linear bottlenecks between the layers and shortcut connections between the bottlenecks. These features not only reduce the model size and computational cost, but also address the problem of information loss in traditional convolutional networks.

This paper presents a novel approach to blind facial image quality enhancement using non-rigid semantic patches. The study focuses on improving the quality of facial images that are degraded due to various factors such as low resolution, noise, and poor lighting conditions. The proposed method involves the use of non-rigid semantic patches, which are flexible and adaptable to different facial structures and expressions. The method is blind, meaning it does not require any prior knowledge about the degradation process. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both subjective and objective evaluations. The paper also discusses potential applications of this method in fields such as facial recognition, image editing, and social media.

This paper introduces EMDS-5, the fifth version of the Environmental Microorganism Image Dataset, designed for multiple image analysis tasks. The dataset comprises a diverse collection of microscopic images of environmental microorganisms, collected from various sources and environments. The paper discusses the improvements made over the previous versions, including increased image quality, diversity, and quantity. It also presents the potential applications of EMDS-5 in various fields such as environmental science, microbiology, and computer vision. The paper further demonstrates the utility of the dataset by conducting several image analysis tasks, including image classification, segmentation, and detection. The results indicate that EMDS-5 can effectively facilitate the development and evaluation of image analysis algorithms in the context of environmental microorganism studies.

This paper presents a novel approach to foreground object detection using unsupervised learning techniques. The study aims to overcome the limitations of supervised learning methods, which require extensive labeled data and may not generalize well to unseen scenarios. The proposed method leverages the inherent structure of video data to learn a model of the foreground object without any manual annotation. The algorithm is based on a combination of deep learning and probabilistic graphical models, which allows it to capture complex object structures and dynamics. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting and segmenting foreground objects, outperforming state-of-the-art supervised methods in terms of accuracy and robustness. The study opens up new avenues for unsupervised learning in video analysis and computer vision applications.

This paper presents a novel approach to training Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) from incomplete observations using factorised discriminators. The study addresses the challenge of training GANs with missing data, which is a common issue in real-world datasets. The proposed method involves the use of factorised discriminators that can handle incomplete observations by learning to factorise the joint distribution of observed and missing data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both the quality of generated samples and the stability of training. The paper also provides theoretical insights into the properties of factorised discriminators and their implications for GAN training. This research opens up new possibilities for the application of GANs in scenarios where data incompleteness is a significant concern.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on Multitask Diffusion Adaptation over Networks. The research focuses on the development and analysis of a distributed algorithm for multitask diffusion adaptation over networks. The algorithm is designed to allow nodes in a network to collaboratively solve a set of related tasks by sharing information with their neighbors. The paper provides a detailed theoretical analysis of the algorithm's convergence and stability properties. It also presents simulation results that demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness in various multitask learning scenarios. The findings suggest that the proposed algorithm can significantly improve the performance of multitask learning in networked systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to the Normalized Least Mean Square (NLMS) algorithm by incorporating a time-variant optimum stepsize derived from a Bayesian network perspective. The study aims to improve the performance of the NLMS algorithm in adaptive filtering applications. The proposed method uses Bayesian networks to model the statistical dependencies between the input signal, the desired response, and the adaptive filter coefficients. This model is then used to derive an optimal time-variant stepsize for the NLMS algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the conventional NLMS algorithm in terms of convergence speed and steady-state error, particularly in non-stationary environments. This research provides a new perspective on the design of adaptive filters and contributes to the field of signal processing.

This paper presents a novel semi-supervised fuzzy GrowCut algorithm for the segmentation and classification of regions of interest (ROIs) in mammographic images. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of breast cancer detection in mammography. The algorithm integrates the advantages of semi-supervised learning and fuzzy logic, providing a more robust and reliable segmentation process. It also incorporates a classification mechanism to identify benign and malignant lesions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, classification performance, and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of computer-aided diagnosis systems in mammography, potentially improving early detection and treatment of breast cancer.

This paper presents a novel network structure designed to explicitly reduce confusion errors in semantic segmentation. Semantic segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, often suffers from confusion errors due to the high similarity between certain classes. To address this issue, we propose a new network structure that incorporates a confusion-aware module. This module is designed to learn the confusion patterns between classes and then guide the network to pay more attention to confusing areas. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our proposed network structure significantly reduces confusion errors and improves the overall performance of semantic segmentation. This research provides a new perspective on improving semantic segmentation and has potential applications in various fields such as autonomous driving, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper delves into the intricate concepts of expansivity and shadowing within the realm of linear dynamics. It aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of these phenomena and their implications in the study of dynamical systems. The paper first elucidates the theoretical underpinnings of expansivity and shadowing, followed by an exploration of their interplay in linear dynamics. It further investigates the conditions under which a linear dynamical system exhibits expansivity and the existence of shadowing. The paper also presents various examples and counterexamples to illustrate these concepts. The findings contribute to the broader understanding of the behavior of linear dynamical systems and open up new avenues for future research.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using Learning Automata (LA) to seek multi-thresholds. Image segmentation is a crucial step in image processing and computer vision, and the selection of appropriate thresholds is a significant challenge. The proposed method employs LA to adaptively find the optimal multi-thresholds for image segmentation. The LA-based algorithm is designed to learn from the environment and adjust the thresholds dynamically, improving the segmentation quality. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional image segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research opens up new possibilities for the application of LA in image processing and computer vision.

This paper presents novel definitions of exponential, hyperbolic, and trigonometric functions on time scales. The study aims to bridge the gap between continuous and discrete analysis by introducing a unified theory that encompasses both fields. The new definitions are based on the forward jump operator and the graininess function, which are fundamental concepts in time scale calculus. The properties of these functions are explored, and their potential applications in various fields, including physics, engineering, and economics, are discussed. The paper also provides proofs to support the new definitions and their properties. The results contribute to the ongoing development of time scale calculus and open up new avenues for future research.

This paper presents a novel approach to partitioning problems using large-margin metric learning. The study introduces a new algorithm that learns a distance metric from a given set of partitioned data, aiming to maximize the margin between different partitions. The proposed method is based on the concept of large-margin classifiers in machine learning, which has been successfully applied in various fields such as image recognition and text categorization. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through several experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing partitioning algorithms in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research opens up new possibilities for solving complex partitioning problems in various domains.

This paper presents a novel approach to minimize annotation costs in medical image segmentation using Suggestive Mixed Supervision Fully Convolutional Networks (SMS-FCN). The proposed method leverages both weakly and strongly annotated data, reducing the need for extensive manual annotation. The SMS-FCN model is designed to suggest regions for strong annotation, thereby optimizing the trade-off between annotation cost and segmentation performance. Experimental results on several medical imaging datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces annotation costs while maintaining competitive segmentation accuracy. This research has potential implications for cost-effective, large-scale medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to data augmentation for one-shot medical image segmentation using learned transformations. The study addresses the challenge of limited annotated medical images for training deep learning models. The proposed method involves learning transformations from the available data and applying these transformations to augment the training set. The effectiveness of this approach is evaluated on several medical imaging datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to traditional data augmentation techniques. The results suggest that the proposed method can effectively leverage limited data to enhance the performance of one-shot medical image segmentation models. This research has potential implications for improving the efficiency and accuracy of medical image analysis in clinical settings.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation of 3D Magnetic Resonance (MR) images, termed as Holistic Decomposition Convolution (HDC). The HDC method aims to address the challenges of complex spatial dependencies and intricate structures in 3D MR images. The proposed method decomposes the 3D convolution into three consecutive 1D convolutions, reducing computational complexity while maintaining the ability to capture 3D contextual information. HDC also incorporates a holistic feature fusion strategy to effectively integrate multi-level features. Extensive experiments on several public datasets demonstrate that HDC outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. The results suggest that HDC could be a promising tool for semantic segmentation in 3D medical image analysis.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on Uniform Information Segmentation (UIS), a novel approach to data analysis. UIS is a method that aims to segment information uniformly, ensuring equal distribution and representation of data. This paper discusses the theoretical underpinnings of UIS, its potential applications, and the challenges associated with its implementation. The study also includes a comparative analysis of UIS with other segmentation methods, highlighting its advantages and potential drawbacks. The results indicate that UIS can significantly improve data analysis outcomes, particularly in large datasets, by ensuring a more balanced and equitable representation of information. However, the paper also underscores the need for further research to optimize UIS and address its limitations.

This paper presents a novel approach to segmenting meaningful objects from Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images using a multi-scale non-local active contour model. The proposed model addresses the challenges of speckle noise and complex structures in SAR images, which often hinder accurate segmentation. The model integrates multi-scale non-local means filtering and active contour methods to enhance the segmentation performance. The multi-scale approach allows the model to adapt to different scales of objects, while the non-local means filtering reduces speckle noise. The active contour method is used to accurately delineate object boundaries. Experimental results on various SAR images demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in segmenting meaningful objects with high accuracy and robustness against noise.

This paper presents a novel generic ensemble-based deep convolutional neural network (CNN) for semi-supervised medical image segmentation. The proposed method leverages the strengths of ensemble learning and deep CNNs to improve the accuracy and robustness of medical image segmentation tasks. The model is designed to handle limited labeled data scenarios, a common issue in medical imaging. The ensemble approach integrates multiple CNN models to reduce the risk of overfitting and enhance generalization capabilities. Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. This study contributes to the advancement of semi-supervised learning techniques in medical image analysis, potentially improving diagnostic accuracy and patient care.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of atrous convolution in semantic image segmentation. We propose a novel approach that rethinks the use of atrous convolution, aiming to improve the accuracy and efficiency of semantic image segmentation. Our method involves a multi-scale context aggregation mechanism that captures image details at various scales without losing resolution. We also introduce a novel module, the Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP), which enhances the model's ability to handle objects of different scales. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. This study provides new insights into the design of effective and efficient deep learning models for semantic image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to instance segmentation using a weakly supervised hybrid network. The proposed method addresses the challenge of requiring large amounts of pixel-level annotations for training in traditional instance segmentation methods. The hybrid network combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with a graph-based model to leverage both local and global contextual information. The CNN is trained with image-level labels, while the graph-based model is used to infer instance-level predictions. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to fully supervised methods, highlighting its effectiveness and potential for practical applications. This research opens up new possibilities for instance segmentation in scenarios where only weak supervision is available.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the quantum phase-space representation for curved configuration spaces. The research explores the Wigner-Weyl formalism, a quantum mechanical framework, and its application to curved spaces. The paper introduces a new approach to quantum mechanics that incorporates geometric quantization and coherent states. The study also investigates the challenges and potential solutions in implementing this approach. The results demonstrate the potential of this representation for providing new insights into quantum mechanics and its applications in various fields, including quantum gravity and quantum cosmology. The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of these findings for future research.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the dual formulation of boosting algorithms. Boosting algorithms are powerful machine learning techniques used for regression and classification tasks. The paper explores the mathematical underpinnings of these algorithms, focusing on their dual formulation. The dual perspective provides a deeper understanding of the nature of boosting algorithms, revealing their connections to support vector machines and other related methods. The paper also discusses the implications of the dual formulation for algorithm design and performance analysis. The findings of this study contribute to the theoretical understanding of boosting algorithms and offer insights that can guide the development of more efficient and effective machine learning methods.

This paper presents a novel approach to constructing set-valued fundamental diagrams from jamiton solutions in second order traffic models. The study focuses on the mathematical modeling of traffic flow, specifically the propagation of traffic jams, known as jamitons. The paper introduces a new method to derive set-valued fundamental diagrams, which are essential tools in traffic flow theory, from these jamiton solutions. The proposed method is based on the concept of multi-valuedness, which allows for a more accurate representation of traffic flow dynamics. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in capturing the complex dynamics of traffic flow, including the formation and propagation of traffic jams. This research contributes to the advancement of traffic flow theory and has potential applications in traffic management and control.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using scribbles as input, leveraging multi-scale adversarial attention gates. The proposed method aims to address the challenges of insufficient and imprecise annotations in medical image segmentation. The model employs a multi-scale strategy to capture features at various scales and an adversarial attention mechanism to focus on challenging regions. The adversarial training strategy is used to enhance the discriminative capability of the model. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming state-of-the-art scribble-based segmentation methods. The study also shows that the model can effectively learn from scribbles and generate high-quality segmentation results, providing a promising solution for practical applications in medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel approach to Pneumothrax segmentation using deep learning image segmentation techniques. Pneumothorax, a condition characterized by collapsed lungs, is typically diagnosed through radiographic imaging. However, the interpretation of these images can be challenging due to the subtle nature of the signs. Our study proposes a deep learning model that can accurately segment and predict Pneumothorax from chest X-ray images. The model was trained and validated on a large dataset of annotated images, demonstrating high accuracy and efficiency. This research could potentially revolutionize the diagnosis process, making it faster and more reliable, thereby improving patient outcomes.

This paper presents a novel approach to binary classification problems by maximizing the linear-fractional utility. The study introduces a calibrated surrogate loss function that is designed to optimize the linear-fractional utility directly. The proposed method is theoretically justified and empirically validated. Theoretical analysis shows that the surrogate loss function is consistent with the linear-fractional utility, and empirical results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional methods in various binary classification tasks. The paper also provides an efficient algorithm for solving the optimization problem associated with the surrogate loss function. This research contributes to the field of machine learning by providing a new perspective on binary classification problems and offering a practical tool for improving classification performance.

This paper presents a novel interpretation of differential privacy, a widely adopted privacy standard, from a Bayesian perspective. We propose a Bayesian formulation of differential privacy that provides a semantic interpretation of the privacy guarantee. This interpretation is based on the posterior predictive distribution, which quantifies the uncertainty about an individual's private information given the differentially private output. We demonstrate that our Bayesian differential privacy satisfies the same worst-case privacy guarantee as the classical differential privacy. Furthermore, we show that it provides a more informative privacy measure in the average case, which can be used to design more efficient privacy-preserving algorithms. Our results bridge the gap between the worst-case privacy guarantee and the average-case privacy risk, and provide a new perspective on understanding and applying differential privacy.

This paper presents Co-Seg, a novel image segmentation framework designed to combat label corruption. Label corruption, a common issue in image segmentation, can significantly degrade the performance of segmentation models. Co-Seg addresses this problem by integrating a label correction mechanism into the segmentation process. The framework leverages a dual-branch architecture, with one branch focusing on segmentation and the other on label correction. The two branches are trained simultaneously, allowing the model to learn robust segmentation features while correcting erroneous labels. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that Co-Seg significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, particularly in scenarios with high label corruption rates.

This paper introduces MISSFormer, a novel transformer-based model for medical image segmentation. The model leverages the self-attention mechanism of transformers to capture long-range dependencies in medical images, which is crucial for accurate segmentation. We propose a new architecture that integrates the transformer with a U-Net-like structure, allowing the model to effectively learn both local and global features. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that MISSFormer outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy, robustness, and efficiency. Furthermore, the model shows excellent generalization ability when applied to different types of medical images. The results suggest that the transformer has great potential in medical image analysis and that MISSFormer can serve as a powerful tool for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to fish recognition, combining robust feature selection, image segmentation, and geometrical parameter techniques. The proposed method utilizes Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) and Decision Trees (DT) to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of fish species identification. The study begins with image segmentation to isolate the fish from its background, followed by feature extraction to identify unique characteristics. The extracted features are then optimized using a robust feature selection technique. Finally, the ANN and DT algorithms are employed to classify the fish species. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the recognition accuracy compared to existing techniques, offering a promising tool for marine biodiversity studies and fisheries management.

This paper presents a novel approach to body schema estimation using Bayesian inference and tactile information obtained through coordinated random movements. The study proposes a probabilistic model that integrates sensory data from different body parts to estimate the body schema. The model is based on the Bayesian framework, which allows for the incorporation of prior knowledge and uncertainty in the estimation process. The tactile information is obtained through coordinated random movements, which provide a rich and diverse set of sensory inputs. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through a series of experiments on a humanoid robot. The results show that the robot can successfully learn its body schema and adapt to changes in its body structure.

This paper investigates the effectiveness of iris recognition in cases of eye pathology. Iris recognition is a biometric identification method that uses mathematical pattern-recognition techniques on video images of the irises of an individual's eyes. However, its accuracy in cases of eye pathology, such as cataracts, glaucoma, or retinal diseases, is not well-studied. This study aims to fill this gap by analyzing the performance of iris recognition algorithms on a dataset of individuals with various eye pathologies. The results indicate that certain pathologies significantly affect the accuracy of iris recognition, suggesting the need for further improvements in the technology. This research has implications for the development of more robust biometric identification systems and for the understanding of how eye diseases may impact such systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on camera pose estimation using deep learning techniques. Camera pose estimation is a crucial task in computer vision, with applications in robotics, augmented reality, and 3D reconstruction. Traditional methods often rely on hand-crafted features and geometric models, which can be sensitive to noise and occlusions. In contrast, deep learning-based methods have shown promising results due to their ability to learn robust features from large amounts of data. This paper provides an overview of the fundamental concepts, methodologies, and challenges in camera pose estimation with deep learning. It also reviews recent advancements and discusses potential future directions in this field.

This paper presents an in-depth study on reflection methods for submodular optimization, aiming to enhance user-friendliness. Submodular functions are widely used in various fields such as machine learning, computer vision, and network design due to their inherent ability to model diminishing returns. However, optimizing these functions can be computationally challenging. This paper introduces novel reflection methods for submodular optimization, which are designed to be more intuitive and user-friendly. The proposed methods are based on the concept of reflection, which transforms a difficult optimization problem into a simpler one. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed methods.

This paper presents a novel multi-contrast Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) approach for thalamus segmentation. The thalamus, a crucial part of the human brain, has been challenging to segment due to its complex structure and the presence of surrounding tissues with similar intensity profiles. The proposed method leverages the complementary information from different MRI contrasts to improve the segmentation accuracy. The approach was tested on a dataset of healthy subjects and patients with various neurological disorders. The results demonstrate that the multi-contrast MRI approach significantly outperforms single-contrast methods, providing more accurate and robust thalamus segmentation. This advancement could potentially enhance the understanding of the thalamus's role in various neurological disorders and improve the effectiveness of related treatments.

This paper introduces PP-LinkNet, a novel approach to improve the semantic segmentation of high-resolution satellite imagery. The proposed method incorporates multi-stage training to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation. The PP-LinkNet model is designed to address the challenges of complex and diverse patterns in satellite images, which traditional segmentation models often struggle with. The multi-stage training strategy involves initial coarse segmentation followed by fine-tuning, which significantly improves the model's performance. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that PP-LinkNet outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of remote sensing image analysis and has potential applications in various fields such as urban planning, environmental monitoring, and disaster management.

This paper presents a novel approach to domain adaptation for image segmentation, termed Source-Relaxed Domain Adaptation (SRDA). The primary focus is on addressing the issue of performance degradation when the distribution of source and target domains differ significantly. SRDA operates by relaxing the reliance on source domain and instead, emphasizes learning transferable features from both source and target domains. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing domain adaptation methods. The results demonstrate that SRDA significantly improves the segmentation performance in the target domain, even when the source and target domains are substantially different. This study contributes to the ongoing research in domain adaptation and image segmentation, providing a new perspective and methodology for tackling domain shift problems.

This paper presents a novel approach to community detection in megascale networks using information-based replica correlations. The method employs a multiresolution technique that allows for the identification of communities at different scales, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the network structure. The proposed algorithm is based on the principle of information theory and utilizes replica correlations to detect communities. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through its application to various real-world networks, including social networks, biological networks, and the internet. The results show that the proposed method can accurately detect communities in megascale networks, outperforming existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the field of network science by providing a scalable and accurate method for community detection in large-scale networks.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the analysis of timed systems using tree automata. The research focuses on the application of tree automata in modeling and analyzing timed systems, which are systems where the behavior depends on quantitative timing information. The paper introduces a novel approach that combines the theory of timed automata with the theory of tree automata, resulting in a powerful tool for analyzing timed systems. The proposed method is demonstrated through various examples and case studies, showing its effectiveness and efficiency. The results indicate that tree automata can provide a more precise and scalable analysis of timed systems compared to traditional methods. This research opens up new avenues for the application of tree automata in the field of timed systems analysis.
