This paper presents a novel approach to improve the performance of semantic segmentation for robot perception by leveraging synthetic data feature transfer to mitigate bias. The study addresses the challenge of real-world data bias in semantic segmentation models, which often leads to sub-optimal robot perception. We propose a synthetic data feature transfer method that utilizes the rich and unbiased feature representation from synthetic data to enhance the model's generalization capability. Our approach involves training a feature extractor on synthetic data and transferring these features to a real-world data model. Experimental results on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly improves the segmentation accuracy and robustness of robot perception systems, outperforming existing state-of-the-art techniques. This research opens up new possibilities for enhancing robot perception using synthetic data, contributing to the advancement of autonomous systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive system-level numerical analysis of a Monte Carlo simulation of the E. Coli chemotaxis. The study aims to understand the behavior and movement of E. Coli bacteria in response to chemical stimuli in their environment. The Monte Carlo simulation, a statistical technique that allows for the modeling of complex biological systems, is used to simulate the chemotaxis process. The paper discusses the simulation model, the parameters used, and the results obtained. The findings provide valuable insights into the chemotactic behavior of E. Coli, which can be instrumental in the development of new strategies for controlling bacterial infections. The paper also highlights the potential of Monte Carlo simulations in studying complex biological systems.

This paper presents an improved algorithm for the vertex cover P3 problem on graphs of bounded treewidth. The vertex cover P3 problem is a well-known combinatorial optimization problem in graph theory, which has been extensively studied due to its theoretical and practical significance. The proposed algorithm improves upon existing methods by reducing the computational complexity and increasing the efficiency of finding the minimum vertex cover. The algorithm is based on dynamic programming and tree decomposition techniques. Theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm performs better than existing methods, especially for graphs with larger treewidth. This research contributes to the field of graph theory by providing a more efficient solution to the vertex cover P3 problem.

This paper investigates the length and area spectrum of analytic convex domains. It delves into the mathematical intricacies of these domains, exploring their geometric and topological properties. The study provides a comprehensive analysis of the length spectrum, which is the set of lengths of closed geodesics, and the area spectrum, which is the set of areas of minimal surfaces. The paper also discusses the relationship between these two spectra and the geometry of the convex domain. The results reveal a deep connection between the geometry of the domain and the properties of these spectra, providing new insights into the structure of analytic convex domains. The findings have potential implications for various fields, including differential geometry, mathematical physics, and complex analysis.

This paper introduces SUSAN, a novel approach to segment unannotated image structures using an adversarial network. The study aims to address the challenge of segmenting complex structures in unannotated images, which is a significant problem in computer vision. SUSAN employs a generative adversarial network (GAN) to learn the underlying structure of unannotated images and effectively segment them. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing methods. The results demonstrate that SUSAN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency, proving its effectiveness in segmenting unannotated image structures. This research opens up new possibilities for image segmentation in various applications, including medical imaging, autonomous driving, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the equivalence of multi-letter quantum finite automata (QFA). We delve into the theoretical aspects of QFA, focusing on the equivalence problem, which is a fundamental question in automata theory. We provide a detailed analysis of the conditions under which two multi-letter QFAs can be considered equivalent. Our findings reveal that the equivalence of multi-letter QFAs is undecidable, which is a significant departure from the classical deterministic finite automata. We also present a series of results that provide a deeper understanding of the structure and behavior of multi-letter QFAs. These results contribute to the ongoing research in quantum computing and automata theory, and open up new avenues for future investigations.

This paper presents a novel approach to medical image segmentation using multi-label deep supervision. The study argues that every annotation in medical imaging, regardless of its complexity, carries significant information for the learning process. The proposed method leverages all available annotations in a multi-label fashion, allowing the model to learn from simple to complex structures simultaneously. The results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves the segmentation performance compared to traditional single-label deep supervision methods. The study also shows that the proposed method is more efficient in terms of computational resources and training time. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis, potentially leading to more accurate diagnoses and better patient outcomes.

This paper presents U-Net, a novel convolutional network architecture for biomedical image segmentation. U-Net is designed to work with very few training images and yields more precise segmentation results. The architecture consists of a contracting path to capture context and a symmetric expanding path that enables precise localization. We have demonstrated that U-Net outperforms prior best methods on the ISBI challenge for segmentation of neuronal structures in electron microscopic stacks. Furthermore, U-Net has been successfully applied to segment not only cells but also various other biomedical image types. The network is fast, efficient, and requires significantly less annotated images, making it a powerful tool for a wide range of biomedical image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on parameter learning for log-supermodular (L-SM) distributions. L-SM distributions are a class of probability distributions that have found significant applications in various fields such as machine learning, computer vision, and statistical physics. Despite their wide applicability, the problem of parameter learning for L-SM distributions has not been thoroughly investigated. This paper fills this gap by providing a detailed analysis of the problem and proposing efficient algorithms for parameter learning. The proposed algorithms are based on convex optimization and are proven to have strong theoretical guarantees. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is demonstrated through extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.

This paper introduces the Inhomogeneity Estimation by Orthogonal Primary Functions (IEOPF), a novel active contour model for image segmentation. The model is designed to handle images with inhomogeneities, a common challenge in image processing. The IEOPF model employs orthogonal primary functions to estimate the inhomogeneity, which is then incorporated into the energy functional of the active contour model. The proposed model is tested on synthetic and real images, demonstrating its effectiveness in segmenting images with inhomogeneities. The results show that the IEOPF model outperforms existing models in terms of accuracy and robustness. This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a new approach to handle inhomogeneities in image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to detecting missing method calls in object-oriented programming by considering them as violations of the majority rule. The majority rule, in this context, refers to the common practice of calling certain methods together in a specific sequence. The proposed technique uses static analysis to identify these common patterns and detect deviations. The paper discusses the implementation of this approach and evaluates its effectiveness using several open-source software systems. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively identify missing method calls, thereby improving code quality and reducing debugging time. The paper also highlights potential areas for further research and improvement.

This paper presents a novel approach to citrus segmentation by integrating supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of citrus segmentation, a critical task in automated citrus harvesting and grading systems. The proposed method first employs unsupervised learning to cluster the citrus pixels based on color and texture features. Then, supervised learning is used to classify the clustered pixels into citrus and non-citrus categories. Experimental results on various citrus datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of automatic citrus harvesting and grading systems, potentially leading to significant improvements in productivity and cost-effectiveness.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the accuracy of Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) segmentation with hidden Potts and Markov mesh prior models. The study employs three different algorithms: Path Constrained Viterbi Training (PCVT), Iterated Conditional Modes (ICM), and Graph Cut based algorithms. The paper provides a detailed comparison of these algorithms in terms of their performance and accuracy in MAP segmentation. The results indicate that the accuracy of MAP segmentation significantly depends on the choice of the algorithm. The paper also discusses the strengths and weaknesses of each algorithm, providing valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of image processing and computer vision. The findings of this study can guide the selection of appropriate algorithms for MAP segmentation tasks in various applications.

This paper presents the third part of a study on modelling galaxy spectra in the presence of interstellar dust. The focus is on extending the models developed for nearby galaxies to the distant Universe. The paper discusses the challenges and complexities of this extension, including the need to account for variations in dust properties and the effects of cosmic evolution. The models are tested against observational data from both nearby and distant galaxies, demonstrating their applicability across a wide range of redshifts. The results provide new insights into the role of dust in shaping galaxy spectra and the evolution of galaxies over cosmic time. The models also offer a valuable tool for interpreting future observations of distant galaxies.

This paper presents a novel approach to ultra-high resolution image segmentation by leveraging locality-aware contextual correlation. The study proposes a new model that integrates both global and local contexts to enhance the accuracy of image segmentation. The model is designed to handle ultra-high resolution images, which are often challenging due to their large size and complex details. The proposed method is based on the concept of locality-awareness, which allows the model to focus on specific regions of the image, thereby improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the segmentation process. The paper also introduces a new correlation mechanism that captures the contextual relationships within and between local regions. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency, making it a promising solution for ultra-high resolution image segmentation.

This paper introduces Sem-GAN, a novel approach to image-to-image translation that ensures semantic consistency between the input and output images. Sem-GAN leverages the power of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and incorporates a semantic consistency loss function to maintain the semantic information during the translation process. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art methods. The results demonstrate that Sem-GAN significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of both visual quality and semantic consistency. Furthermore, the proposed method is robust to changes in the input images and can handle a wide range of translation tasks. This paper provides a new perspective on image-to-image translation and opens up new possibilities for future research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to video semantic segmentation using Clockwork Convnets. The proposed method leverages the temporal redundancy present in videos to reduce the computational cost of segmentation without compromising the quality of results. The Clockwork Convnets operate by selectively updating certain parts of the network at different rates based on the complexity and variability of the video content. This approach allows for efficient processing of video data, making it suitable for real-time applications. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable or superior performance to existing methods while significantly reducing computational requirements. This work contributes to the field of computer vision by providing a more efficient method for video semantic segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to 3D medical image segmentation using an attention-guided active learning strategy. The proposed method aims to reduce the need for extensive manual annotations, a common challenge in medical image analysis. The strategy employs a sparse annotation technique, which leverages the attention mechanism to identify critical regions in the images. Active learning is then used to iteratively train the segmentation model, improving its performance with each iteration. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly reduces the annotation effort while maintaining high segmentation accuracy. This work has potential implications for improving efficiency in medical image analysis and could be applied to various medical imaging modalities.

This paper presents a novel approach to object segmentation in images, focusing on personal fixations-based object segmentation. The proposed method combines object localization and boundary preservation techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of object segmentation. The study introduces a new algorithm that uses personal fixations data to guide the segmentation process, effectively identifying and isolating objects of interest in complex scenes. The algorithm also incorporates boundary preservation techniques to maintain the integrity of object shapes. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for various applications, including image editing, computer vision, and human-computer interaction.

This paper presents a comprehensive comparative study of various statistical skin detection algorithms applied to sub-continental human images. The study aims to evaluate the performance and accuracy of these algorithms in detecting and segmenting skin regions in images from diverse ethnic backgrounds, specifically focusing on sub-continental populations. The algorithms under study include Gaussian Mixture Models, Bayesian Classifier, Support Vector Machines, and Artificial Neural Networks. The evaluation is based on several metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy. The results provide valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each algorithm, offering guidance for future research and development in skin detection technology. The study also highlights the need for more inclusive and diverse datasets in the field of skin detection.

This paper presents a novel approach for Out-of-Distribution (OOD) detection in multi-label datasets using the latent space of $β$-Variational Autoencoder ($β$-VAE). The study focuses on the challenge of identifying OOD samples in multi-label datasets, which is a critical task in machine learning and data analysis. The proposed method leverages the properties of $β$-VAE, a type of generative model, to map the data into a lower-dimensional latent space. This mapping is then used to distinguish between in-distribution and OOD samples. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in detecting OOD samples, outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods. The paper also discusses potential applications and future directions for this research.

This paper introduces a novel measure of economic complexity that is simple, intuitive, and robust. The measure is based on the diversity of products a country produces and the ubiquity of these products across countries. The paper argues that this measure is a significant predictor of economic growth and income inequality. It also demonstrates that countries with higher economic complexity have more stable economies and are better equipped to withstand economic shocks. The paper further explores the implications of economic complexity for economic policy and development strategies. The findings suggest that promoting economic complexity can be a viable strategy for sustainable economic development and reducing income inequality.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using reinforced active learning. The study proposes a new algorithm that combines the strengths of reinforcement learning and active learning to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation. The algorithm uses reinforcement learning to make decisions about which data to learn from, and active learning to iteratively refine the model based on these decisions. The proposed method is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with state-of-the-art image segmentation methods. The results demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the performance of image segmentation tasks, reducing errors and increasing speed. This research opens up new possibilities for the application of reinforced active learning in image analysis and computer vision.

This paper explores the potential of quantum cryptography beyond the widely studied Quantum Key Distribution (QKD). While QKD has been the primary focus of quantum cryptography research, this paper argues that there are other promising applications that deserve attention. These include Quantum Money, Quantum Digital Signatures, and Quantum Secret Sharing. The paper provides an overview of these applications, discussing their potential benefits and challenges. It also highlights the need for further research in these areas to fully realize the potential of quantum cryptography. The paper concludes by emphasizing the importance of exploring quantum cryptography beyond QKD, as it could lead to more secure and efficient cryptographic systems.

This paper presents a novel approach to hyperspectral unmixing using collaborative sparse regression with spatially correlated supports. Hyperspectral unmixing is a critical task in remote sensing, aiming to identify and quantify the constituent materials of each pixel in a hyperspectral image. Traditional methods often fail to consider the spatial correlation of the materials, leading to suboptimal results. To address this issue, we propose a collaborative sparse regression model that incorporates spatial correlation into the unmixing process. The model leverages the spatial correlation of the materials' distribution to enhance the unmixing performance. Experimental results on both synthetic and real hyperspectral data demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in improving the accuracy of hyperspectral unmixing.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using an autoregressive unsupervised learning model. The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial dependencies in images to generate accurate and coherent segmentations without the need for manual annotation. The model is trained on a large dataset of diverse images, allowing it to generalize well to unseen data. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. Furthermore, the autoregressive nature of the model allows for the generation of multiple plausible segmentations for a given image, providing a measure of uncertainty in the segmentation process. This work has potential applications in a variety of fields, including computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the automatic segmentation of teeth in X-ray images, a critical task in dental diagnostics and treatment planning. We review the current trends and methodologies in this field, highlighting the challenges and limitations of existing approaches. To facilitate future research, we introduce a novel dataset of annotated dental X-ray images. We also provide a benchmarking of various state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms on this dataset, offering insights into their performance and applicability in real-world scenarios. Finally, we discuss potential future directions in this area, emphasizing the need for more robust and accurate segmentation techniques. This work aims to stimulate further research and development in automatic teeth segmentation, ultimately contributing to improved dental healthcare.

This paper presents a novel self-learning Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for skin lesion image segmentation and classification. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of skin cancer diagnosis by automating the process of identifying and classifying skin lesions. The proposed framework utilizes deep learning algorithms for image segmentation, feature extraction, and classification. The results demonstrate that the self-learning AI framework outperforms existing methods in terms of accuracy, precision, and recall. The framework also exhibits robustness against variations in image quality and lesion characteristics. This research contributes to the field of medical imaging and AI, offering potential for early and accurate skin cancer diagnosis, thereby improving patient outcomes.

This paper explores the extensions of Lie algebras of differential operators. It delves into the theory of Lie algebras, focusing on the differential operators and their extensions. The paper provides a comprehensive study of the structure and properties of these extensions, including their cohomology and representation theory. It also discusses the applications of these extensions in various fields of mathematics and theoretical physics. The paper presents new methods and results, contributing to the understanding of the complex structure and behavior of Lie algebras of differential operators. The findings of this study have potential implications for further research in the field.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the automated design of deep learning methods for biomedical image segmentation. The research focuses on the development and evaluation of novel algorithms that can automatically generate effective deep learning models, eliminating the need for manual design and tuning. The proposed methods are based on reinforcement learning and genetic algorithms, which are used to search the vast space of possible model architectures. The performance of these automated methods is evaluated on several biomedical image segmentation tasks, including the segmentation of brain tumors, lung nodules, and cells in microscopy images. The results demonstrate that the automatically designed models can achieve comparable or even superior performance to manually designed models, while significantly reducing the time and effort required for model design. This study suggests that automated design of deep learning methods holds great potential for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of biomedical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised adaptation method for multi-modal cardiac image segmentation using point-clouds and entropy minimisation. The proposed method, named Adapt Everywhere, addresses the challenge of domain shift in medical imaging, which often leads to a significant drop in the performance of segmentation models. The method leverages the inherent structure of point-clouds to adapt the model to new domains without requiring any labelled data. Furthermore, it employs entropy minimisation to ensure the consistency of predictions across different modalities. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Adapt Everywhere, outperforming state-of-the-art unsupervised domain adaptation methods in terms of segmentation accuracy and robustness to domain shift. The results suggest that the proposed method can be a promising tool for improving the performance of cardiac image segmentation in clinical practice.

This paper presents a novel linear framework for region-based image segmentation and inpainting that incorporates curvature penalization. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image processing tasks by considering the curvature information of the image regions. The framework is based on a variational approach and uses a level set method for image segmentation and a partial differential equation for image inpainting. The curvature penalization term is introduced to preserve the smoothness and continuity of the image structures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation and inpainting quality, particularly in dealing with images containing complex structures and textures. The linear nature of the framework also ensures computational efficiency, making it suitable for real-time applications.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the modeling and control of an active constrained layer (ACL) beam actuated by two voltage sources, considering both scenarios with and without magnetic effects. The ACL beam is a smart structure that has been widely used in vibration control applications. The mathematical model of the ACL beam is derived using Hamilton's principle and the assumed mode method. The influence of magnetic effects on the beam's dynamic behavior is also investigated. Two control strategies, namely, the optimal control and the sliding mode control, are designed to suppress the vibration of the ACL beam. Numerical simulations are conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed models and control strategies.

This paper presents a novel approach to video semantic segmentation, a critical task in computer vision, by integrating labels propagation and refinement. The proposed method aims to improve efficiency and accuracy by leveraging temporal coherence in videos. The algorithm first propagates labels from keyframes to non-keyframes, then refines the segmentation results using a lightweight network. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy. Furthermore, the proposed method is computationally efficient, making it suitable for real-time applications. This research contributes to the advancement of video semantic segmentation techniques and has potential implications for various applications such as autonomous driving, video surveillance, and human-computer interaction.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using Cellular Automata (CA). Image segmentation is a crucial process in image analysis and computer vision, which partitions an image into multiple segments to simplify and/or change the representation into something more meaningful and easier to analyze. The proposed method leverages the dynamic behavior of CA, a discrete computational model, to perform image segmentation. The paper discusses the principles of CA, the design of the proposed CA-based image segmentation method, and its implementation. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional image segmentation techniques in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also explores potential applications of the CA-based image segmentation in various fields such as medical imaging, remote sensing, and object recognition.

This paper delves into the intricacies of Euclid's Algorithm, a cornerstone of elementary number theory, and its various applications. The study begins with a comprehensive overview of the algorithm's historical development and its fundamental principles. It then explores the algorithm's role in determining the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two integers, highlighting its efficiency and computational simplicity. The paper further discusses the algorithm's extension to the Euclidean domain and its implications for the broader field of number theory. The study also presents various proofs and mathematical models to elucidate the algorithm's workings and its connection to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic. The paper concludes with a discussion on the algorithm's modern applications, including cryptography and coding theory.

This paper presents a novel approach for unsupervised segmentation of 3D medical images using clustering and deep representation learning. The proposed method does not require any prior knowledge or training data, making it highly applicable in scenarios where annotated data is scarce or unavailable. The method first extracts deep features from the 3D medical images using a pre-trained 3D convolutional neural network. Then, a clustering algorithm is applied to group similar features together, forming distinct segments. Experimental results on various types of medical images, including MRI and CT scans, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately segmenting different anatomical structures. The proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation methods, showing its potential for practical applications in medical image analysis.

This paper presents a novel Generalized Asymmetric Dual-front Model (GADM) for active contours and image segmentation. The proposed model is designed to handle complex segmentation tasks, including those with weak boundaries, noise, and intensity inhomogeneity. The GADM is based on a dual-front strategy, which allows it to capture both the interior and exterior boundaries of objects. The model also incorporates an asymmetric speed function to handle intensity inhomogeneity and a regularization term to suppress noise. Experimental results on synthetic and real images demonstrate the superior performance of the GADM in terms of accuracy, robustness, and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art methods. The GADM has potential applications in various fields, including medical imaging, computer vision, and pattern recognition.

This paper presents a novel active set algorithm for estimating parameters in generalized linear models (GLMs) with ordered predictors. The algorithm is designed to handle the unique challenges posed by ordered predictors, such as the need for monotonicity constraints. The proposed method is based on a quadratic approximation of the log-likelihood function, which allows for efficient computation and robust performance. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of simulation studies and real data applications. The results show that the proposed method provides accurate parameter estimates and outperforms existing methods in terms of computational efficiency and stability. This research contributes to the field of statistical modeling by offering a new tool for handling GLMs with ordered predictors.

This paper presents an innovative approach to automatic color image segmentation using a square elemental region-based seeded region growing and merging method. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques by incorporating a square elemental region-based approach, which enhances the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. The method begins with an initial segmentation into square elemental regions, followed by a seeded region growing process, and finally a merging process to combine similar regions. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using various color images, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high-quality segmentation results. The method is robust, computationally efficient, and capable of handling images with complex structures and varying textures. This research contributes to the field of image processing by providing a novel method for automatic color image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel approach to image co-segmentation using deep metric learning. Image co-segmentation, the task of segmenting common objects from a set of images, is a challenging problem in computer vision. Traditional methods often fail to capture the complex variations in object appearance. To address this, we propose a deep metric learning-based method that learns a similarity metric between image regions, enabling the model to identify common objects more accurately. Our method leverages a deep convolutional neural network to extract robust features and a metric learning layer to learn the similarity. Extensive experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

This paper presents a novel Meta Segmentation Network (MSN) for ultra-resolution medical images. The proposed MSN addresses the challenges of high computational cost and memory consumption associated with processing ultra-resolution images. It employs a meta-learning approach that adapts to new tasks with minimal training data, making it suitable for medical applications where annotated data is scarce. The MSN also incorporates a multi-scale feature fusion module to capture both local and global context information, enhancing the segmentation performance. Extensive experiments on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate that the MSN outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. The proposed network has potential applications in various medical imaging tasks, including disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a novel approach to solving the crystallographic phase problem using dynamical scattering in electron diffraction. The phase problem, a fundamental challenge in crystallography, involves determining the phase of a wave when only its intensity can be measured. Our method leverages the unique properties of dynamical scattering in electron diffraction to extract phase information. We provide a comprehensive theoretical framework for this approach, supported by experimental data from various crystal structures. The results demonstrate that our method can accurately retrieve phase information, offering a promising solution to the phase problem. This could significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of crystal structure determination, with potential applications in materials science, chemistry, and biology.

This paper presents a novel approach to multi-label segmentation of medical images with lesions using dynamic multiscale tree learning and ensemble strong classifiers. The proposed method addresses the challenges of accurately identifying and classifying multiple types of lesions in medical images, which is crucial for effective diagnosis and treatment planning. The dynamic multiscale tree learning algorithm is designed to adaptively learn and adjust to the complexity and diversity of the lesions. The ensemble strong classifiers further enhance the segmentation performance by integrating the decisions of multiple weak classifiers. Experimental results on various types of medical images demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis and has potential applications in computer-aided diagnosis and personalized medicine.

This paper presents a novel method for multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) brain image segmentation based on differential geometric features. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of brain image segmentation, a critical process in diagnosing and treating neurological disorders. The paper first introduces the concept of differential geometry and its application in image processing. It then details the proposed segmentation method, which involves extracting differential geometric features from multimodal MRI brain images and using these features to segment the images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. This research has significant implications for the development of more effective diagnostic tools in neurology.

This paper presents a novel approach to the segmentation of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI using Deep 3D Fully Convolutional DenseNets. The proposed method employs exclusive independent probability estimation to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of the segmentation process. The DenseNets architecture is utilized to extract and fuse high-level features from different scales, which significantly improves the discriminative capability of the model. The exclusive independent probability estimation further refines the segmentation results by considering the exclusive relationship among different classes. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This study provides a promising tool for the automatic and accurate segmentation of IsoIntense Infant Brain MRI, which is crucial for the early diagnosis and treatment of various neurological disorders.

This paper investigates gridless sparse methods for line spectral estimation from both complete and incomplete data. The study focuses on the application of these methods in signal processing, particularly in spectral analysis. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the performance of these methods, highlighting their advantages and limitations. It also proposes novel techniques to improve the accuracy and efficiency of line spectral estimation. The results demonstrate that gridless sparse methods can effectively estimate spectral lines from incomplete data, providing a robust solution for practical applications in signal processing. The paper concludes with suggestions for future research to further optimize these methods.

This paper presents a comprehensive quantitative test of general theories of the intrinsic laser linewidth. The study involves a detailed examination of the Schawlow-Townes linewidth formula, which has been a cornerstone in the understanding of laser linewidths. The paper also explores the Henry alpha factor, which is crucial in determining the linewidth enhancement factor. The experimental results obtained from various types of lasers, including semiconductor and fiber lasers, are compared with theoretical predictions. The findings reveal a significant discrepancy between the experimental results and the predictions of the Schawlow-Townes formula, suggesting the need for a more comprehensive theory. The paper concludes with a discussion on the implications of these findings for future research in laser technology and quantum optics.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the modeling and semigroup formulation of charge or current-controlled active constrained layer (ACL) beams. The research focuses on three assumptions: electrostatic, quasi-static, and fully-dynamic. The paper first introduces the mathematical modeling of ACL beams, followed by the development of a semigroup formulation. The electrostatic assumption simplifies the model by neglecting the time variation of electric fields, while the quasi-static assumption considers slow time variations. The fully-dynamic assumption, on the other hand, takes into account all time variations. The results of this study provide a deeper understanding of the behavior of ACL beams under different assumptions and contribute to the optimization of their control and performance.

This academic paper presents a novel approach to gaze estimation, a critical aspect of human-computer interaction. Traditionally, gaze estimation has been focused on the eye region, but this paper proposes a full-face appearance-based method. The study demonstrates that the entire face contributes to gaze direction and that utilizing full-face information significantly improves gaze estimation accuracy. The paper also introduces a new large-scale dataset for gaze estimation, collected under diverse conditions. The results show that the proposed method outperforms existing eye-based methods, particularly in real-world, unconstrained environments. This research has significant implications for the development of more natural and efficient human-computer interaction systems.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on efficient algorithms for scheduling moldable tasks. Moldable tasks are computational tasks that can be executed on different numbers of processors. The paper introduces novel algorithms that optimize the scheduling of these tasks, aiming to minimize the overall completion time. The algorithms are based on advanced mathematical models and are designed to be adaptable to various computing environments. The paper also includes a comparative analysis of the proposed algorithms with existing ones, demonstrating their superior efficiency and adaptability. The results of this study have significant implications for high-performance computing, cloud computing, and other areas where efficient task scheduling is critical.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic segmentation using RGBD sensing, with a focus on incremental class discovery. Traditional methods of semantic segmentation are limited by their inability to adapt to new classes after training. Our proposed method overcomes this limitation by incorporating an incremental learning framework that allows the model to learn new classes without forgetting the previously learned ones. We introduce a new RGBD dataset for semantic segmentation, which includes a diverse set of classes. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of accuracy and adaptability. This research opens up new possibilities for real-world applications of semantic segmentation, particularly in dynamic environments where the set of object classes can change over time.

This paper investigates the collective spontaneous emission from a system of quantum dots. Quantum dots, nanoscale semiconductor particles, exhibit unique optical and electronic properties due to their quantum confinement, making them ideal for studying quantum phenomena. We explore the collective behavior of these quantum dots under specific conditions, focusing on their spontaneous emission - a fundamental quantum process where an excited quantum system relaxes to its ground state by emitting a photon. Our study reveals that the collective spontaneous emission can be significantly enhanced compared to the emission from individual quantum dots. This finding has potential implications for the development of quantum information technologies, including quantum computing and quantum communication. The paper also discusses the theoretical framework, experimental setup, and potential applications of our findings.

This paper presents a novel approach to optimization problems using Chebyshev polynomials. The study explores the mathematical properties of Chebyshev polynomials and their potential application in optimization algorithms. The paper introduces a new method that leverages the unique characteristics of these polynomials to improve the efficiency and accuracy of solving complex optimization problems. The proposed method is tested on several benchmark problems and compared with traditional optimization techniques. The results demonstrate that the Chebyshev polynomial-based method provides superior performance in terms of speed and solution quality. This research opens up new avenues for the use of Chebyshev polynomials in various optimization scenarios.

This paper presents a novel approach to volumetric medical image segmentation using Positional Contrastive Learning (PCL). The proposed method leverages the inherent spatial information in volumetric images to enhance the segmentation performance. PCL is designed to learn discriminative features by contrasting positive and negative samples based on their spatial positions. The effectiveness of PCL is evaluated on several benchmark datasets of different medical imaging modalities, including CT and MRI scans. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art segmentation methods in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency. This study suggests that PCL can be a promising tool for improving the quality of medical image analysis, which is crucial for accurate disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents a comprehensive study of nominal unification from a higher-order perspective. It delves into the intricacies of nominal unification, a process crucial in various fields such as computational linguistics, automated reasoning, and programming languages. The study explores the theoretical underpinnings of nominal unification, its applications, and its limitations. It also introduces a novel approach to nominal unification, which leverages higher-order logic to address some of the challenges associated with traditional methods. The paper further provides a comparative analysis of the proposed method with existing techniques, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency. The findings of this study contribute to the broader understanding of nominal unification and open new avenues for future research in this area.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation, termed Hierarchical Piecewise-Constant Super-regions (HPCS). The HPCS method aims to overcome the limitations of existing segmentation techniques by providing a more accurate and detailed representation of an image. The proposed method works by dividing an image into a hierarchy of super-regions, each of which is characterized by a piecewise-constant intensity profile. The hierarchical nature of the method allows for a flexible and adaptive representation of the image, capturing both fine and coarse details. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the HPCS method in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The proposed method has potential applications in various fields, including computer vision, image processing, and medical imaging.

This paper presents a novel approach to iris recognition using image segmentation and retrained off-the-shelf deep neural networks. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of iris recognition systems, which are crucial in biometric identification. The proposed method involves the use of pre-existing deep learning models, which are retrained to adapt to iris recognition tasks. The paper discusses the process of image segmentation, feature extraction, and classification in detail. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional iris recognition techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy. The study also highlights the potential of deep learning in enhancing the performance of biometric systems.

This paper presents a study on the optical addressing of an individual erbium ion in silicon. The research explores the potential of erbium ions as quantum bits in silicon-based quantum computers. The study demonstrates the ability to isolate and manipulate a single erbium ion embedded in silicon, using optical methods. The results show that the ion can be addressed individually, paving the way for its use in quantum information processing. The paper also discusses the challenges faced in the process and potential solutions. The findings of this research contribute significantly to the development of silicon-based quantum computing technology.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using nonparametric shape priors. The method employs Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) shape sampling, which allows for a more flexible and accurate representation of shape variations. The proposed technique is particularly effective in handling images with complex shapes and high levels of noise. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. The paper also provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of different shape prior models on the segmentation results. This research contributes to the field of image processing by introducing a robust and efficient method for image segmentation with nonparametric shape priors.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of deep learning techniques for object saliency detection and image segmentation. We propose a novel deep learning model that effectively identifies the most visually significant objects in an image and accurately segments them from the background. The model is trained and tested on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing methods. The paper also provides an in-depth analysis of the model's performance, highlighting its robustness and efficiency. Furthermore, we discuss potential improvements and future directions for research in this field. This work contributes to the advancement of computer vision technologies and has potential applications in various fields such as autonomous driving, robotics, and surveillance systems.

This paper introduces w-Net, a novel dual supervised medical image segmentation model that incorporates multi-dimensional attention and cascade multi-scale convolution. The model aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of medical image segmentation, a critical task in medical image analysis. The proposed w-Net model employs a dual supervision mechanism to guide the learning process, enhancing the model's ability to capture intricate details and complex structures in medical images. Furthermore, the model integrates a multi-dimensional attention mechanism to focus on significant features and suppress irrelevant ones. It also utilizes a cascade multi-scale convolution to extract features at different scales effectively. Experimental results on various medical image datasets demonstrate that the proposed w-Net model outperforms existing state-of-the-art segmentation models in terms of accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency.

This paper presents a novel approach to unssupervised image segmentation using global and local criteria optimization based on Bayesian Networks. The proposed method aims to overcome the limitations of traditional image segmentation techniques, which often fail to accurately segment complex images due to the lack of prior knowledge. Our approach integrates global and local criteria into a unified Bayesian framework, allowing for the optimization of both criteria simultaneously. The global criterion ensures the overall coherence of the segmentation, while the local criterion preserves the details of the image. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in producing high-quality segmentation results, outperforming several state-of-the-art techniques. This research opens up new possibilities for improving image segmentation in various applications, including computer vision, medical imaging, and remote sensing.

This paper investigates the role of uncertainty estimation in active learning for image segmentation. It presents a comprehensive study on various uncertainty estimation methods and their impact on the performance of active learning algorithms. The paper introduces a novel approach for uncertainty estimation that significantly improves the accuracy of image segmentation. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The paper also discusses the challenges and potential future directions in this research area. The findings of this study provide valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in the field of computer vision and machine learning, particularly those working on active learning and image segmentation.

This paper presents a novel, efficient semidefinite programming (SDP) approach to solving binary quadratic problems (BQP). BQP, a NP-hard problem, has wide applications in various fields such as machine learning, operations research, and computer vision. Traditional methods often suffer from high computational complexity or poor solution quality. Our proposed method leverages the power of SDP relaxation to provide a fast and high-quality solution to BQP. We demonstrate the superiority of our approach through extensive computational experiments on various benchmark instances. The results show that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms in terms of both solution quality and computational efficiency.

This paper investigates the well-posedness and robust preconditioners for discretized fluid-structure interaction (FSI) systems. FSI systems are complex and challenging to solve due to the coupling of fluid and solid domains. The paper first establishes the well-posedness of the discretized FSI system under certain conditions. It then proposes robust preconditioners to improve the efficiency and stability of the iterative solution process. Numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical results and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioners. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the numerical solution of FSI problems and have potential applications in various fields such as engineering, physics, and biology.

This paper presents a novel approach to semantic image segmentation using StyleGAN and CLIP, two state-of-the-art machine learning models. The proposed method is unsupervised, eliminating the need for large, manually annotated datasets. The paper demonstrates how StyleGAN can generate diverse and high-quality images, while CLIP can understand and interpret these images in a semantic context. The combination of these models allows for effective segmentation of images into semantically meaningful regions. Experimental results show that our approach outperforms existing unsupervised segmentation methods in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research opens up new possibilities for image analysis and understanding, with potential applications in various fields such as computer vision, robotics, and autonomous driving.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of Deep Learning (DL) architectures for nuclear image segmentation in generalized immunofluorescence. The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of nuclear image segmentation, a critical process in the analysis of cellular structures and functions. We explore various DL architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and their variants. The paper also discusses the implementation of these architectures, their performance comparison, and the challenges encountered. The results demonstrate that DL architectures significantly enhance the segmentation accuracy compared to traditional methods, thereby providing a promising tool for advanced biomedical research. The paper concludes with future directions for optimizing DL-based nuclear image segmentation.

This paper investigates the phenomenon of overfitting in neural networks, specifically in the context of image segmentation tasks under class imbalance conditions. Overfitting, a common issue in machine learning, occurs when a model learns the training data too well, negatively impacting its performance on unseen data. Class imbalance, another prevalent problem, arises when the number of instances of different classes in a dataset is unequal. We conduct a series of experiments using various neural network architectures and image datasets to understand how class imbalance influences overfitting. Our findings suggest that class imbalance exacerbates overfitting in image segmentation tasks, and we propose several strategies to mitigate this issue. This research contributes to the broader understanding of overfitting in neural networks and provides practical insights for improving model performance in image segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using nonparametric clustering techniques. The study aims to overcome the limitations of traditional parametric methods, which often require a priori knowledge of the number of clusters and their distribution. The proposed method employs a nonparametric clustering algorithm that does not require any assumptions about the data distribution and can automatically determine the number of clusters. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive experiments on various image datasets. The results show that the nonparametric clustering approach provides superior performance in terms of both segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. This research opens up new possibilities for image segmentation, particularly in applications where the number of segments is unknown or varies across images.

This paper introduces CRNet (Cross-Reference Networks), a novel approach for few-shot segmentation. The primary objective of CRNet is to address the challenge of segmenting objects in images with limited annotated examples. CRNet leverages cross-referencing between a support set and a query image to generate more robust and discriminative features. It also introduces a new cross-reference mechanism that enhances the interaction between the support and query features, thereby improving the segmentation performance. Experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that CRNet significantly outperforms existing few-shot segmentation methods, establishing a new state-of-the-art in the field. The paper also provides comprehensive ablation studies to validate the effectiveness of the proposed cross-reference mechanism.

This paper presents a novel approach to sketch colorization using adversarial segmentation loss. The study proposes a new framework that leverages the strengths of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and segmentation networks to improve the colorization of sketches. The proposed method aims to address the common issues in sketch colorization such as color bleeding and lack of detail. The adversarial segmentation loss function encourages the model to generate colorized sketches that are not only visually appealing but also semantically meaningful. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing techniques in terms of both visual quality and quantitative evaluations. This research opens up new possibilities for the application of GANs in sketch colorization and other related fields.

This paper presents a novel approach to the semantic segmentation of motion capture data using Dilated Temporal Fully-Convolutional Networks (DTFCNs). The study aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of motion capture data analysis by introducing a fine-grained segmentation method. The proposed DTFCN model is designed to capture long-range dependencies in the temporal domain, which is crucial for understanding complex human motions. The model is evaluated on several benchmark datasets and compared with existing methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. This research opens up new possibilities for the application of deep learning techniques in motion capture data analysis and related fields.

This paper explores a variant of the classic hat game, known as Ebert's asymmetric three person three color Hat Game. The game involves three players, each wearing a hat of one of three colors, and the objective is to correctly guess the color of one's own hat. The twist in this version is the asymmetric information each player has about the others' hats. The paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the game, including its mathematical model, strategies for optimal play, and implications for game theory. The study reveals that the game's complexity increases significantly with the introduction of asymmetry, leading to intriguing strategic possibilities. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of decision-making processes under uncertainty and asymmetric information.

This paper explores the fascinating world of Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) and Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) through a series of case studies. The aim is to provide a comprehensive understanding of these mathematical concepts and their applications in various fields. The paper begins with a brief introduction to ODEs and PDEs, followed by an in-depth analysis of their solutions. The case studies presented cover a wide range of applications, from physics and engineering to economics and biology, demonstrating the versatility and importance of these mathematical tools. The paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions in the study of ODEs and PDEs. This paper serves as a valuable resource for students, researchers, and professionals interested in the practical applications of differential equations.

This paper presents a novel multi-layer approach to superpixel-based higher-order Conditional Random Field (CRF) for semantic image segmentation. The proposed method aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of image segmentation by leveraging the advantages of superpixels and higher-order CRFs. The multi-layer approach involves the generation of superpixels at different scales, which are then integrated into a higher-order CRF framework. The framework is designed to capture both local and global contextual information, thereby enhancing the segmentation performance. Experimental results on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving superior segmentation accuracy compared to existing methods. The paper also discusses potential applications of this approach in various fields such as computer vision, image processing, and machine learning.

This academic paper explores the intersection of sequential decision problems, dependent types, and generic solutions. It delves into the theoretical underpinnings of sequential decision problems and how they can be effectively solved using dependent types. The paper also introduces a novel approach to developing generic solutions for these problems. The approach is based on the use of dependent types, a concept from type theory, which allows for more precise typing and thus, more efficient and accurate solutions. The paper presents a series of case studies to illustrate the application of this approach. The results demonstrate that the use of dependent types can significantly improve the performance of solutions to sequential decision problems.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on coalgebraic infinite traces and Kleisli simulations. It delves into the theoretical aspects of coalgebra, a branch of mathematics that studies systems by observing their behavior in response to inputs. The paper introduces a novel approach to infinite traces in a coalgebraic setting, providing a new perspective on the concept of state-based systems. It also explores Kleisli simulations, a category-theoretic concept, and its applications in the context of coalgebra. The paper further establishes a connection between these two concepts, offering a deeper understanding of their interplay. The findings of this study contribute to the existing body of knowledge in coalgebra and category theory, and open up new avenues for future research.

This paper presents a novel hierarchical self-supervised learning approach for medical image segmentation, leveraging multi-domain data aggregation. The study aims to address the challenges of limited annotated data and high annotation costs in medical imaging. The proposed method involves a hierarchical learning structure that progressively learns from easy to complex tasks, improving the model's generalization ability. It also incorporates multi-domain data aggregation to enhance the diversity of the training data, thereby improving the robustness of the model. Experimental results on various medical imaging datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, outperforming several state-of-the-art techniques in terms of segmentation accuracy and efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of self-supervised learning techniques in the field of medical image analysis, with potential applications in disease diagnosis and treatment planning.

This paper presents an in-depth study on recursive quantum repeater networks. Quantum repeaters are pivotal in long-distance quantum communication, enhancing the transmission fidelity and extending the communication distance. This study introduces a novel recursive structure for quantum repeater networks, which significantly improves the efficiency and scalability of quantum communication systems. The recursive design allows for a more flexible and robust network, capable of adapting to various communication demands and error rates. Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate the superiority of the proposed recursive network over traditional linear repeater chains in terms of communication rate and distance. This research opens up new avenues for the design and implementation of large-scale quantum networks.

This paper presents a novel approach to edge detection using structured forests, a machine learning technique. The proposed method significantly improves the speed and accuracy of edge detection in digital images. The structured forests algorithm is trained on a large dataset of manually annotated images, enabling it to learn and generalize the characteristics of edges. The algorithm is then applied to new images, rapidly identifying edges with a high degree of precision. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing edge detection techniques in terms of both speed and accuracy. This research has potential applications in a wide range of fields, including computer vision, image processing, and artificial intelligence.

This paper presents a novel model for the heating of the Solar North Polar Coronal Hole (SNPCH). The model is based on the analysis of high-resolution solar observations and incorporates the latest advancements in solar physics. The proposed model suggests a unique heating mechanism that is driven by the magnetic reconnection of the coronal magnetic field lines. The model successfully reproduces the observed temperature and density profiles of the SNPCH, providing a better understanding of the physical processes occurring in this region. The results have significant implications for solar wind acceleration and space weather prediction. The model also offers new insights into the fundamental processes of solar coronal heating, which remains one of the most challenging problems in astrophysics.

This paper presents a novel approach to abdominal multi-organ segmentation using voxel-level Siamese representation learning. The study aims to address the challenges of inter-subject and intra-subject variability in abdominal organ segmentation. The proposed method leverages a Siamese network to learn a voxel-level representation that captures the anatomical context of each voxel, thereby improving the segmentation performance. The network is trained using a novel loss function that encourages the learning of similar representations for voxels belonging to the same organ and different representations for voxels from different organs. Experimental results on a publicly available dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving the accuracy and consistency of abdominal multi-organ segmentation. The study contributes to the field of medical image analysis by providing a new perspective on representation learning for organ segmentation tasks.

This paper presents a novel image segmentation enhancement technique that combines active contour and topological alignments. Image segmentation is a crucial process in various fields such as medical imaging, computer vision, and pattern recognition. However, traditional methods often struggle with issues such as noise interference and boundary leakage. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative technique that integrates active contour models, known for their robustness against noise, with topological alignments, which provide accurate boundary detection. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms existing techniques in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and noise resistance. This research opens new avenues for improving image segmentation quality and has potential applications in numerous domains.

This paper presents a comprehensive study on improving learning effectiveness for object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds. The research focuses on developing advanced machine learning algorithms that can accurately identify and classify objects in complex and cluttered environments. The proposed methods aim to overcome the challenges of occlusion, varying object scales, and high intra-class variability. The paper introduces a novel approach that combines deep learning techniques with traditional image processing methods to enhance the performance of object detection and classification systems. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves the accuracy and robustness of object detection and classification in cluttered backgrounds compared to existing methods. This research has potential applications in various fields, including autonomous driving, surveillance, and robotics.

This paper investigates the reduction of ion heating during magnetic reconnection by large-scale effective potentials. Magnetic reconnection, a fundamental process in plasma physics, often leads to significant ion heating. However, the mechanisms behind this phenomenon remain unclear. This study presents a novel approach to understanding and mitigating ion heating during magnetic reconnection. By employing large-scale effective potentials, we demonstrate a significant reduction in ion heating. Our findings provide valuable insights into the control of ion heating in magnetic reconnection, with potential applications in fusion energy research and space physics.

A multilayer surface detector for ultracold neutrons (UCNs) is described. The
top $^{10}$B layer is exposed to the vacuum chamber and directly captures UCNs.
 The ZnS: Ag layer beneath the $^{10}$B layer is a few microns thick, which is
sufficient to detect the charged particles from the $^{10}$B(n,$\alpha$)$^7$Li
neutron-capture reaction, while thin enough so that ample light due to $\alpha$
and $^7$Li escapes for detection by photomultiplier tubes. One-hundred-nm thick
$^{10}$B layer gives high UCN detection efficiency, as determined by the mean
UCN kinetic energy, detector materials and others. Low background, including
negligible sensitivity to ambient neutrons, has also been verified through
pulse-shape analysis and comparisons with other existing $^3$He and $^{10}$B
detectors.

Pixelwise segmentation of the left ventricular (LV) myocardium and the four
cardiac chambers in 2-D steady state free precession (SSFP) cine sequences is
an essential preprocessing step for a wide range of analyses. Variability in
contrast, appearance, orientation, and placement of the heart between patients,
clinical views, scanners, and protocols makes fully automatic semantic
segmentation a notoriously difficult problem. Here, we present ${\Omega}$-Net
(Omega-Net): a novel convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture for
simultaneous localization, transformation into a canonical orientation, and
semantic segmentation. First, an initial segmentation is performed on the input
image, second, the features learned during this initial segmentation are used
to predict the parameters needed to transform the input image into a canonical
orientation, and third, a final segmentation is performed on the transformed
image. In this work, ${\Omega}$-Nets of varying depths were trained to detect
five foreground classes in any of three clinical views (short axis, SA,
four-chamber, 4C, two-chamber, 2C), without prior knowledge of the view being
segmented. The architecture was trained on a cohort of patients with
hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and healthy control subjects.

Current image segmentation techniques usually require that the user tune
several parameters in order to obtain maximum segmentation accuracy, a
computationally inefficient approach, especially when a large number of images
must be processed sequentially in daily practice. The use of evolving fuzzy
systems for designing a method that automatically adjusts parameters to segment
medical images according to the quality expectation of expert users has been
proposed recently (Evolving fuzzy image segmentation EFIS). However, EFIS
suffers from a few limitations when used in practice mainly due to some fixed
parameters. For instance, EFIS depends on auto-detection of the object of
interest for feature calculation, a task that is highly application-dependent.
 This shortcoming limits the applicability of EFIS, which was proposed with the
ultimate goal of offering a generic but adjustable segmentation scheme. In this
paper, a new version of EFIS is proposed to overcome these limitations.

Deep learning methods have achieved promising performance in many areas, but
they are still struggling with noisy-labeled images during the training
process. Considering that the annotation quality indispensably relies on great
expertise, the problem is even more crucial in the medical image domain. How to
eliminate the disturbance from noisy labels for segmentation tasks without
further annotations is still a significant challenge. In this paper, we
introduce our label quality evaluation strategy for deep neural networks
automatically assessing the quality of each label, which is not explicitly
provided, and training on clean-annotated ones. We propose a solution for
network automatically evaluating the relative quality of the labels in the
training set and using good ones to tune the network parameters. We also design
an overfitting control module to let the network maximally learn from the
precise annotations during the training process.

This paper presents a novel unsupervised domain adaptation framework, called
Synergistic Image and Feature Adaptation (SIFA), to effectively tackle the
problem of domain shift. Domain adaptation has become an important and hot
topic in recent studies on deep learning, aiming to recover performance
degradation when applying the neural networks to new testing domains. Our
proposed SIFA is an elegant learning diagram which presents synergistic fusion
of adaptations from both image and feature perspectives. In particular, we
simultaneously transform the appearance of images across domains and enhance
domain-invariance of the extracted features towards the segmentation task. The
feature encoder layers are shared by both perspectives to grasp their mutual
benefits during the end-to-end learning procedure. Without using any annotation
from the target domain, the learning of our unified model is guided by
adversarial losses, with multiple discriminators employed from various aspects.

Interactive single-image segmentation is ubiquitous in the scientific and
commercial imaging software. In this work, we focus on the single-image
segmentation problem only with some seeds such as scribbles. Inspired by the
dynamic receptive field in the human being's visual system, we propose the
Gaussian dynamic convolution (GDC) to fast and efficiently aggregate the
contextual information for neural networks. The core idea is randomly selecting
the spatial sampling area according to the Gaussian distribution offsets. Our
GDC can be easily used as a module to build lightweight or complex segmentation
networks. We adopt the proposed GDC to address the typical single-image
segmentation tasks.

Recently, there has been focus on penalized log-likelihood covariance
estimation for sparse inverse covariance (precision) matrices. The penalty is
responsible for inducing sparsity, and a very common choice is the convex $l_1$
norm. However, the best estimator performance is not always achieved with this
penalty. The most natural sparsity promoting "norm" is the non-convex $l_0$
penalty but its lack of convexity has deterred its use in sparse maximum
likelihood estimation. In this paper we consider non-convex $l_0$ penalized
log-likelihood inverse covariance estimation and present a novel cyclic descent
algorithm for its optimization. Convergence to a local minimizer is proved,
which is highly non-trivial, and we demonstrate via simulations the reduced
bias and superior quality of the $l_0$ penalty as compared to the $l_1$
penalty.

We study type one generalized complex and generalized Calabi--Yau manifolds.
 We introduce a cohomology class that obstructs the existence of a globally
defined, closed 2-form which agrees with the symplectic form on the leaves of
the generalized complex structure, the twisting class. We prove that in a
compact, type one, 4n-dimensional generalized complex manifold the Euler
characteristic must be even and equal to the signature modulo four. The
generalized Calabi--Yau condition places much stronger constrains: a compact
type one generalized Calabi--Yau fibers over the 2-torus and if the structure
has one compact leaf, then this fibration can be chosen to be the fibration by
the symplectic leaves of the generalized complex structure. If the twisting
class vanishes, one can always deform the structure so that it has a compact
leaf.

We propose a single chain slip-spring model, which is based on the
slip-spring model by Likhtman [A. E. Likhtman, Macromolecules, 38, 6128
(2005)], for fast rheology simulations of entangled polymers on a GPU. We
modify the original slip-spring model slightly for efficient calculations on a
